title: 第一章　为什么是社会主义？

第一部
起源
en:
I
THE ORIGINS

children: 第一个圈起一块土地、想到说“这是我的”，并且找到足够单纯的人相信他的人，便是市民社会的真正奠基者。假如有人拔掉木桩、填平沟壑，向自己的同类喊道：“不要听信这个骗子！如果你们忘记土地的果实属于大家、土地不属于任何人，你们就完了！”——人类本来可以免除多少罪恶、战争、杀戮和恐怖啊！

The first man who, having enclosed a piece of land, took it into his head to say, “This is mine,” and found people simple enough to believe him, was the true founder of civil society. The human race would have been spared endless crimes, wars, murders, and horrors if someone had pulled up the stakes or filled in the ditch and cried out to his fellow man, “Do not listen to this imposter! You are lost if you forget that the fruits of the earth belong to everyone, and the earth to no one!”
——让-雅克·卢梭，《论人类不平等的起源和基础》，1752年
—J. J. Rousseau, Discourse on the Origin of Inequality, 1752

The gradual development of the principle of equality is … a Providential fact … it is universal, it is durable, it constantly eludes all human interference, and all men as well as all events contribute to its progress

——阿列克西·德·托克维尔，《论美国的民主》，1835年

zh: 俄国革命之所以值得注意，与其说是因为它是俄国的——尽管在俄国发生一场普通的“资产阶级”革命本身也会是一件大事——不如说是因为它把世界上第一个社会主义政府送上了台。但成为社会主义者意味着什么？我们又能依据什么标准来判断十月政权是否确实造就了一个社会主义社会？或者，就此而言，是否真有哪个社会主义政府真正配得上这个名称？
en: The Russian Revolution is noteworthy not so much because it was Russian—though an ordinary “bourgeois” revolution in Russia would have been quite an event—but because it brought the world’s first socialist government to power. But what does it mean to be socialist? And by what standards can we judge whether the October regime in fact produced a socialist society? Or whether any socialist government, for that matter, has ever truly merited its name?

zh: 社会主义：民主的最高阶段
en: SOCIALISM: THE HIGHEST STAGE OF DEMOCRACY

zh: 在现代政治词汇中，没有哪个词比“社会主义”更充满歧义、更牵动情感。对大多数人来说，就其最宽泛的含义而言，这个词指的是与“资本主义”不同的一种组织经济的方法。在这个意义上，社会主义指的是具体的制度安排和政府计划。然而，这类组织形式的范围如此之广，以至于这个词很快就失去了焦点；当我们从累进税制和“安全网”式的社会保障，走到从摇篮到坟墓的福利国家，再走到整个经济的彻底国有化和计划化时，这一点就显而易见了。那么，也许可以在市场与计划这一宽泛的对立中，为资本主义—社会主义这一对立找到稳定的含义？
en: No word in the modern political vocabulary is more fraught with ambiguity or charged with emotion than “socialism.” For most people, and in its broadest meaning, the term designates an alternative method to “capitalism” for organizing the economy. In this sense, socialism refers to concrete institutional arrangements and governmental programs. Yet the gamut of these organizational forms is such that the term quickly loses focus; this is clearly evident as we move from progressive taxation and “safety-net” social security to a cradle-to-the-grave welfare state, on to outright nationalization and planning of the entire economy. So perhaps a stable meaning for the antithesis capitalism-socialism can be found in the broad notion of market versus plan?

zh: 但这也不是一个稳定的焦点。因为在社会主义的用法中，市场被视为“无政府的”，计划被视为“理性的”，而这些说法又给分析蒙上了一层规范性的光环。进一步探究只会扩大这一规范领域，因为社会主义还意味着集体主义对立于个人主义、合作对立于竞争、社会服务对立于追逐利润、利他主义对立于贪婪。因此，社会主义最终意味着一个公正而人道的社会，其本质成为一种道德理念，而不是任何制度或经济纲领。
en: But this is not a stable focus either. For in socialist usage the market is held to be “anarchic” and the plan “rational,” and these terms give a normative aura to the analysis. Further probing only expands this normative area, for socialism also means collectivism as opposed to individualism, cooperation as opposed to competition, social service as opposed to profit seeking, and altruism as opposed to greed. Thus socialism means, ultimately, a just and humane society, and its essence becomes a moral idea rather than any institutional or economic program.

zh: 但这仍未穷尽社会主义含义的多样性。这个词还指一种独特的社会形态，如“社会主义社会”与“资本主义社会”的对立，而这两个术语都被认为涵盖了一切人类活动——政治的、经济的、文化的，甚至个人的——并将其纳入一个单一的整体系统。在这个意义上，作为公正而人道制度的社会主义，不仅是资本主义的替代方案，而且“高于”资本主义。于是，社会主义也意味着历史的顶点、人类发展的目的；在这种形态下，它产生了一种历史理论，或者逐渐融入所谓元历史或“历史哲学”。
en: But this still does not exhaust socialism’s multiplicity of meanings. The word also designates a distinctive social formation, as in the antithesis “socialist society” versus “capitalist society,” and both terms are seen as encompassing all human activity—political, economic, cultural, and even personal—in a single, total system. In this sense, socialism, as the just and humane system, is not just an alternative to, but is “higher” than, capitalism. So socialism also comes to mean the culmination of history, the telos of human development; in this guise it generates a theory of history, or shades off into what has been called metahistory or “historiosophy.”

zh: 这种含义的混乱，又因各种彼此不相容、却都自称“社会主义”的制度形式而更加严重。因此，斯大林主义的俄国、文化大革命的中国、社会民主党“中间道路”的瑞典、工党的英国、基布兹的以色列、布鲁克农场的合作社区，以及红色高棉，都曾貌似有理地声称拥有这个词。而且，这些形形色色的社会主义通常都质疑其他社会主义的合法性，事实上还常常以尖锐的宗派腔调诅咒自己的对手。
en: This confusion of meanings is still worse confounded by the variety of mutually incompatible institutional forms that have called themselves “socialist.” Thus the term has been plausibly claimed by Stalinist Russia, China of the Cultural Revolution, Sweden of the Social Democratic “middle way,” Labourite Britain, Israel of the Kibbutzim, the cooperative community of Brook Farm, and the Khmer Rouge. These various socialisms, moreover, have usually challenged the legitimacy of the others, and indeed have often anathematized their rivals in shrill sectarian tones.

zh: 另一个基本的含义混乱来自“在野的社会主义”与“执政的社会主义”之间的区别。在前一种情况下，我们面对的是一个为有组织地追求更人道社会而存在的运动，它通过政党、工会、合作社或类似的兄弟般的事业表达出来。在这种情况下，社会主义是一群追求正义者的道德共同体，他们因其使命而与一个冷漠或敌意的世界区别开来。然而，在执政的社会主义的情况下，我们面对的是一个据称已处于历史终点的既成社会，如同“封建主义、资本主义、社会主义”这一元历史序列所示。但权力众所周知的腐化倾向，总是使这个社会与先前运动的理想之间产生巨大鸿沟。结果是，执政的社会主义常常被仍处反对派的社会主义者谴责为蜕变为“国家社会主义”，甚至更糟的“国家资本主义”。于是，运动又在“具有人道面孔的社会主义”旗帜下重生，而对真正社会主义社会的期待再次被推迟到未来。
en: Still another basic confusion of meaning arises from the difference between “socialism in opposition” and “socialism in power.” In the former case we have a

for the organized pursuit of a more human society, as expressed through political parties, trade unions, cooperatives, or similar fraternal undertakings. In this case socialism is a moral fellowship of seekers after justice, who are set off by their calling from an indifferent or hostile world. In the case of socialism in power, however, we have an established

, allegedly coming at the end of history, as in the metahistorical succession of “feudalism, capitalism, socialism.” But the well-known propensity of power to corrupt invariably produces a great gap between this society and the ideals of the antecedent movement. The result is that socialism in power is often denounced by socialists still in opposition as a degeneration into “state socialism” or, even worse, “state capitalism.” The movement is then reborn under the banner of “socialism with a human face,” and the expectation of the true socialist society is again put off to the future.

zh: 这种对未来的关注，是围绕“社会主义”的歧义的最深层原因；因为在我们所有指称不同类型社会的术语中，唯独“社会主义”是在这类社会存在的事实之前、而非之后被创造出来的。例如，“封建主义”“专制主义”“旧制度”“自由主义”和“资本主义”都出现在其存在的事实之后或同时；因此它们指称某种真实的东西，无论其历史或现实多么不完善地体现了它们所声称的原则。但社会主义一词及其更高阶段的衍生词“共产主义”的独特之处在于，它早在1917年首次尝试实现相应现实之前近一个世纪就已出现。因此，社会主义首先并不指称一个实际的社会形态；它指称的毋宁是对一切现存社会形态的理想替代，而为了这个目的，现存社会形态被标上“资本主义”的标签——这个术语是在其对立面之后才被铸造出来的，并被设计为它的元历史陪衬。总之，社会主义是一个乌托邦，用的是这个词的字面含义：一个被视为理想“他者”的“非场所”或“无处”。
en: This focus on the future is the deepest cause of the ambiguity surrounding “socialism,” for of all our terms designating different types of societies “socialism” alone was created before, not after, the fact of that type of society’s existence. “Feudalism,” “absolutism,” “Old Regime,” “liberalism,” and “capitalism,” for example, all emerged either after or simultaneously with the fact of their existence; they therefore designate something real, however imperfectly their history or reality embodies whatever principles they may claim. But the term socialism, together with its higher derivative, “communism,” is unique in that it appeared almost a century before the first attempt was made, in 1917, to attain a corresponding reality. Thus socialism does not designate in the first instance an actual social formation; it designates rather an ideal alternative to all existing social formations, which are labeled for this purpose “capitalism,” a term coined
its antithesis and designed to serve as its metahistorical foil. In sum, socialism is a utopia, in the literal meaning of that term: a “non-place” or a “no-where” viewed as an ideal “other.”

zh: 因此，“社会主义”一词的独特之处在于，它并不对应尘世中任何可识别、且所有观察者都能就其性质达成一致的对象。诚然，曾有许多错误的目击，也曾有一些一时令人信服的幻影，但没有任何一个产生过只有经验验证才能带来的那种一致意见。所以，社会主义的完整现实被留给了信仰的领域：“对未见之物的信念，对未知之事的希望。”
en: The term socialism is thus unique in that it corresponds to no identifiable object in the sublunary world on whose nature all observers can agree. To he sure, there have been numerous false sightings and some temporarily convincing apparitions, but none has produced that unanimity of opinion that only empirical verification can bring. So, the full reality of socialism is reserved for the realm of faith, “the belief in things unseen, the hope in things unknown.”

zh: 于是可以清楚地看到，严格说来，“社会主义”并不意味任何东西。第一，它在本质上是无意义的，因为其经济纲领未能、也不可能以一种使人不得不承认其为真正社会主义的方式实现其道德理想。第二，它在历史上是无意义的，因为如此众多彼此不相容的社会形态都曾声称拥有它，使它失去了一切具体的焦点。所以，当人们宣称信奉社会主义时，我们永远不知道他们究竟是什么意思，也不知道他们一旦掌权可以指望做什么。这种含糊不清无疑为布尔什维克通向全面权力铺平了道路——也促进了人民阵线不时与他们合作。
en: Thus it becomes clear that “socialism,” strictly speaking, does not mean anything. First, it is meaningless, intrinsically, because its economic programs do not, and cannot, realize its moral ideal in a manner that compels recognition as true socialism. Second, it is meaningless, historically, because it has been claimed by so many mutually incompatible social formations that it loses all concrete focus. So when people profess socialism we never know just what they mean, or what they can be expected to do if they come to power. This imprecision certainly smoothed the Bolsheviks’ way to total power—and eased periodic Popular Front collaboration with them.

zh: 因此，社会主义根本不是一个历史学或社会科学的术语，而最终是一个弥赛亚式的、甚至近乎巫术的术语；事实上，人们常常指出，那些更为狂热的社会主义形式带有某种世俗宗教的色彩。
大批人曾经涌过红场，高呼“向着社会主义的胜利前进！”，但很难想象股东们会沿着华尔街游行，嘴里念叨着关于资本主义的这类振奋人心的口号。而当自由市场的捍卫者用“非共产主义”或“资本主义”宣言来回应马克思时，这不过是徒劳之举，仿佛信仰可以被增长统计数据所击败。
但社会主义观念的威力就是如此之大，以致大多数人——其敌人不亚于其朋友——始终把它误认为一个社会科学范畴或一个据称的历史阶段，从而使我们每当说出“社会主义”时，都陷入持久的混乱。
en: Thus socialism is not a historical or a social-science term at all, but ultimately a messianic, indeed a quasi-magical term; in fact, it has often been claimed that the more ardent forms of socialism have something of a secular religion about them.

Masses of humanity could once surge through Red Square chanting “forward to the victory of socialism!” but it is quite inconceivable that shareholders should march down Wall Street mouthing such rousing slogans about capitalism. And it is an exercise in futility when champions of the free market answer Marx with “Non-Communist” or “Capitalist” Manifestos, as if faith could be vanquished by growth statistics.

But such is the potency of the socialist idea that most men—its foes no less than its friends—perennially mistake it for a social-science category or a putative stage of history, to the enduring confusion of what we are talking about whenever we utter “socialism.”

zh: 社会主义的情感力量来自另一个同样充满激情且含义模糊的术语：“民主”。在二十世纪后期的通常用法中，民主结合了三样在历史上来源不同、且未必相互关联的东西：第一，宪政政府和法治；第二，建立在人民意志之上的主权在民；第三，被理解为社会平等的社会正义。
en: Socialism derives its emotional charge from an equally charged and ambiguous term: “democracy.” In the common usage of the late twentieth century, democracy combines three things that historically have different origins and that are not necessarily related: first, constitutional government and the rule of law; second, popular sovereignty founded on the will of the people; third, social justice understood as social equality.

zh: 其中第一项，即以代议制议会为基础、通过独立司法实现法治的宪政政府，起源于中世纪的封建制度。只提这一发展中最明显、最著名的例子，我们只需回想：英国的《大宪章》并非现代的权利法案，而是国王与其男爵之间的封建契约。同样，议会之母逐渐发展为由世袭贵族组成的议会，另设选举产生的下议院，其成员是同样享有特权的郡骑士和市民代表。简言之，只有绅士参与其中，而广大民众则被视为“农民流氓”或“农奴”（欧洲村民旧时的称呼），被排除在公共生活之外。
en: The first of these, constitutional government based on a representative assembly and the rule of law through an independent judiciary, has its origin in medieval feudal institutions. To mention only the most obvious and best known instances in this development, we need simply recall that England’s Magna Carta was no modern Bill of Rights but a feudal contract between the king and his barons. Likewise, the Mother of Parliaments developed as an assembly of hereditary lords with an elective Commons of equally privileged knights-of-the-shire and burgesses. In short, only gentlemen were involved, while the mass of humanity was dismissed as “peasant rogues” or “villeins” (as European villagers were once known) and excluded from public life.

zh: 直到十八世纪，在美国革命和法国革命中，这种寡头宪政才开始扩展到整个社会。然而，即使在这两场革命中，古希腊词“民主”也几乎从未被使用：几个世纪以来，它已经意味着导致“无政府”的“暴民统治”，而在最初的现代共和国中，绝对平等也不被认为必要，甚至不可行。事实上，直到1863年，建立在男性普选权基础上的美国共和国的彻底宪政秩序，仍被认为可以与动产奴隶制相容。简言之，宪政政府远比主权在民或把正义等同于社会平等古老。
en: It was only in the eighteenth century, in the American and French Revolutions, that this oligarchic constitutionalism began to be generalized to the whole of society. Yet even in those two revolutions, the ancient Greek word “democracy” was almost never used: Over the centuries it had come to mean “mob rule” leading to “anarchy,” and absolute equality was not deemed necessary, or even feasible, in the first modern republics. Indeed, as late as 1863 the thoroughly constitutional order of the American Republic, founded on universal manhood suffrage, was still deemed compatible with chattel slavery. In short, constitutional government is far older than popular sovereignty or the equation of justice with social equality.

zh: 后两项原则直到十八世纪中叶才出现。在此之前，所有欧洲社会（以及非欧洲社会）都建立在另外两项原则之上。第一，合法权威始终是上级权威：它来自上方，通过王权或某种团体合议制行使，而这一切最终由上帝或自然法、或两者共同认可。因此，政府不是由人或社会设计的；它只是被给定的。第二项旧制度原则是，一切社会都必然划分为相互依存但不平等的等级阶层，无论是古罗马贵族与平民、贵族与庶民，还是教士与俗人；因此，不平等是自然的、合法的、不可避免的。
en: The latter two principles appeared only in the middle of the eighteenth century. Until that time all European societies (and non-European ones as well) rested on two other principles. The first was that legitimate authority was always superordinate authority: It came from above and was exercised through kingship or some corporate collegiality, the whole ultimately sanctioned by God or the law of nature or both. Government thus was not devised by man or society; it was simply given. The second old-regime principle was that all societies were necessarily divided into a class hierarchy of interdependent but unequal orders, whether of patricians and plebeians, of nobles and commoners, or of clergy and laity; inequality, therefore, was natural, legitimate, and inevitable.

zh: 对这些古老观念的挑战虽然酝酿已久，但直到十八世纪中叶才首次公开而激烈地爆发。让-雅克·卢梭的《论人类不平等的起源和基础》（1752年）和《社会契约论》（1762年）可以算作这场平等主义革命的主要征兆——当然不是其原因。但很快，上级权威和自然不平等的观念就被视为十足的可耻。例如，正是在这一时期，奴隶制在有记载的历史上第一次开始显得令开明舆论厌恶，废奴主义也作为一个运动兴起。
en: The challenge to these immemorial ideas, though long in gestation, first became open and militant in the mid-eighteenth century. Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s

children: Discourse on the Origin of Inequality

en: (1762) may be counted as the major symptoms, though not of course the cause, of this egalitarian revolution. But soon the ideas of superordinate authority and natural inequality were deemed downright scandalous, For example, it was only in this period that slavery, for the first time in recorded history, came to appear abhorrent to enlightened opinion, and that abolitionism emerged as a movement.

zh: 但只有在美国革命和法国革命中，人们才第一次按照这些新原则行动。美国革命是第一个在实践中确立主权在民的政治运动；不过，它并未明确推进平等主义议程，因为直到1820年代，大多数州仍实行财产资格选举制。随后，法国革命把对旧制度的挑战推进到底，从与财产资格选举制相结合的主权在民，走向更合乎逻辑的男性普选制所体现的平等主义。尽管这一进展被证明是暂时的，但它仍然把普选原则确立为整个欧洲下一个世纪的目标。
en: But it was only in the American and French Revolutions that men first acted on these new principles. The American Revolution was the first political movement to enshrine popular sovereignty in practice; still, it did not explicitly advance an egalitarian agenda, for a property suffrage existed in most states until the 1820s. Then, the French Revolution carried the challenge to the Old Regime all the way by moving from popular sovereignty combined with a property suffrage to the more logical egalitarianism of universal (manhood) suffrage. Though this advance proved temporary, it nonetheless established the principle of universal suffrage as the next century’s goal throughout Europe.

zh: 为什么平等的观念在人类历史上出现得如此之晚，显然是一个复杂的问题，但革命时代的主要思想家提出了一些非常可信的洞见。为新意识——正是这种新意识使平等主义革命成为可能——作出贡献的人太多，无法哪怕粗略地概述，但可以挑出几个关键名字，以体现或象征这个新价值世界最关键的一些方面。
en: Why the idea of equality appeared so recently in human history is obviously a complex matter, but very plausible insights were advanced by the major thinkers of the Revolutionary Age. The number of those who contributed to the new awareness that made the egalitarian revolution possible is too large to permit even a cursory survey, but a few key names may be singled out as epitomizing, or symbolizing, the most crucial aspects of this new world of values.

zh: 如果人与人之间的平等要成为一种首要的道德原则和一种政治力量，它首先必须在物质上成为可能。直到十八世纪后期，这一点才开始成为现实，而这里伟大的象征性名字是亚当·斯密，他的《国富论》与《美国独立宣言》同在1776年问世。在此之前，人类社会的生产能力增长得如此缓慢，几乎难以察觉：每一次增长往往很快就被更大幅度的人口增长所抵消，而人口增长又受到战争、瘟疫和饥荒的抑制——这一模式最早由斯密的批评者托马斯·马尔萨斯加以分析。在这种普遍匮乏的状况下，贫穷的多数从属于富裕而强大的少数，显得不可避免，因而也显得正常而合法。
en: If equality among men were to become a primary moral principle and a political force, it first had to be materially possible. It was only in the late eighteenth century that this began to be true, and here the great symbolic name is Adam Smith, whose

appeared in the same year, 1776, as the American Declaration of Independence. Until this period the productive capacity of human society had increased so slowly as to be almost imperceptible: Every increase tended to be quickly cancelled out by an even greater increase in population, which was then reined in by the scourges of war, pestilence, and famine, a pattern first analyzed by a critic of Smith, Thomas Malthus. Under such circumstances of generalized scarcity, the subordination of the penurious many to the affluent and powerful few appeared unavoidable and, hence, normal and legitimate.

zh: 斯密所做的，是挑战这种宿命论观点。他并不是像今天某些评论者所说的那样，宣告了“资本主义”的到来，因为当时并不存在这样的词或概念；他也没有表现出真正意识到一场工业革命正在他写作时发生，尽管历史学家如今把这场革命视为那个时代的经济核心。毋宁说，他用更符合那个时代的术语论证道，“分工”的发展终于使人类得以进入“商业社会”——这是“狩猎”“畜牧”和“农耕”等较早阶段之后“文明”的顶点。于是，人“互通有无、以物易物、互相交换的天然倾向”终于摆脱了束缚，从而使“公共富裕的扩张”——也就是今天所谓的“增长”——得以加速。
尽管斯密对“自利”的“看不见的手”为所有人谋福利说了很多，但他很少使用“市场”一词，而且只在交换机制或特定需求领域的有限意义上使用，而不是在社会的整体组织的更宽泛意义上使用。对他而言，眼前的实际任务是打击他那个时代的政府的“重商制度”和工人行会——事实上还有企业家的垄断行为——以解放人改善自身道德和物质处境的能力。
en: What Smith did was to challenge this fatalistic view. He did not do this by proclaiming the advent of “capitalism,” as same commentators today would have it, since no such word or concept existed at the time; nor did he express any real awareness of an industrial revolution occurring as he wrote, although historians now make this revolution the economic centerpiece of the period. Rather, in terms more appropriate to the age, he argued that the development of the “division of labor” had at last made it possible for mankind to enter “commercial society,” the “civilized” culmination of a progression whose earlier stages had been “hunting,” “pasturage,” and “farming.” So the natural “propensity of men to barter, truck, and exchange one thing for another” was at last unfettered, thereby making possible an accelerated “expansion of public opulence,” or what would now be called “growth.”

Although Smith had much to say about “the invisible hand” of “self-interest” working for the benefit of all, he used the word “market” sparingly and only in the limited sense of the mechanism of exchange or of a specific area of demand, not in the broader sense of the global organization of society. For him the practical task at hand was to combat the “mercantile system” of the governments and the worker guilds of his day—and, indeed, the monopolistic practices of the entrepreneurs—in order to liberate man’s capacity to improve his moral and material lot.

zh: 正是这种向善论的信息和乐观的唯物论，这种相信“富裕”最终可以惠及大多数人的信念，构成了十九世纪古典自由主义与初生社会主义的共同前提。无论是“资产阶级”还是“无产阶级”的社会主义代言人——商业阶级和劳动阶级在1830年后分别被如此实体化——都分享着对这个新工业时代的基本乐观态度。然而，他们对人类解放所需社会条件的估计却大相径庭。对自由主义者来说，市场——或用十九世纪的说法，“自由贸易”——是进步的动力。但对社会主义者来说，自由贸易和分工意味着强者对弱者的胜利：这些市场力量是社会分化、不平等、剥削以及由此而来的人性丧失的原因。尽管马克思是对斯密式革命持这种悲观看法的最系统、最有力的阐述者，但他并未否定这场革命。对他、对所有社会主义者来说，它是现代性的奠基性行动。正如弗里德里希·恩格斯所说：“亚当·斯密是政治经济学的马丁·路德”，是把人类从重商主义的“中世纪”落后状态中解放出来的人。
en: It is this melioristic message and optimistic materialism, this belief that “opulence” could eventually be available to the larger number of men, that was the precondition for both nineteenth-century classical liberalism and nascent socialism. Both the “bourgeoisie” and the socialist spokesmen for the “proletariat”—as the commercial and laboring classes respectively came to be hypostatized after 1830—shared this fundamental optimism about the new industrial age. They differed mightily, however, in their estimates of the social conditions necessary for human liberation. For liberals it was the market, or, as the nineteenth century put it, “free trade,” that was the motive force of progress. But for socialists free trade and the division of labor meant the victory of the strong over the weak: These market forces were the cause of social differentiation, inequality, exploitation, and, therefore, of dehumanization. Although Marx was the most systematic and powerful exponent of this pessimistic perception of the Smithian revolution, he did not repudiate it. For him, as for all socialists, it was the founding act of modernity. As Friedrich Engels put the matter, “Adam Smith was the Martin Luther of political economy,” the liberator of mankind from the “medieval” backwardness of mercantilism.

zh: 但这种物质变化只有与决定性的文化变化相结合才能生效，后者赋予人对自身在自然和历史中位置的新理解。这一转变的源头是十七世纪的科学革命，它第一次给人类带来了看似无误、至少无可争辩的知识。因为这种知识的革命性在于：它处理的是普遍而必然的规律，且常常以数学方式表达，却仍能通过经验加以验证。于是，人似乎获得了此前只归于上帝的那种绝对知识。因此，下一个世纪的启蒙运动带来了乐观的希望：自然科学的新方法可以扩展到一切人类活动和一切知识分支，产生一种普遍的科学，而这种科学也将成为力量——支配自然、社会和人本身的力量。在这种能动的向善论中，启蒙运动开始把历史视为进步的凯旋行军。
en: But this material change could be effective only in conjunction with decisive cultural changes that conferred on man a new understanding of his place in nature and history. The origin of this transformation was the seventeenth-century’s Scientific Revolution, which for the first time gave mankind what seemed to he infallible, or at least incontrovertible, knowledge. For the revolutionary quality of this knowledge was that while it dealt in universal and necessary laws, often mathematically expressed, it yet could still be verified empirically. Man thus appeared to have acquired absolute knowledge of the sort previously attributed only to God. So the Enlightenment of the next century brought forth the optimistic hope that the new method of the natural sciences could be extended to all human activity and all branches of knowledge to yield a universal science that would also be power—over nature, society, and man himself. And in this dynamic meliorism the Enlightenment came to view history as the triumphal march of Progress.

zh: 但这种新愿景只有通过挑战此前支配欧洲文化的力量——基督教的启示宗教——才能取胜。起初，较为温和的理性主义者，如约翰·洛克，虽然仍对宗教表示敬意，却已把它贬到严格从属的地位。后来，更为极端的理性主义者，如伏尔泰和百科全书派，或大卫·休谟和爱德华·吉本，则用自然理性完全取代了启示宗教。然而，温和与激进的哲人（philosophes）都把理性理解为从感官经验中经验地推导知识，因为这似乎是新科学得以建立的方式。与此同时，这种感觉主义经验论把道德变成了对肉体快乐与痛苦的功利计算。但卢梭是最早指出这一点的人之一：“良心的声音”告诉我们的伦理和“美德”的要义并非如此。
en: But this new vision could win out only by challenging the force that had hitherto dominated European culture, the revealed religion of Christianity. At first, moderate rationalists, such as John Locke, while still deferential to religion, had nonetheless relegated it to a strictly subordinate role. Later, more extreme rationalists, such as Voltaire and the Encyclopedists, or David Hume and Edward Gibbon, replaced revealed religion entirely with natural reason. Yet both moderate and radical

understood reason to mean the empirical derivation of knowledge from sensory experience, since this seemed to be the way the new science had been built up. Concomitantly, this sensationalist empiricism transformed morality into a utilitarian calculus of physical pleasure and pain. But as Rousseau was among the first to emphasize, this is not what the “voice of conscience” tells us ethics and “virtue” arc all about.

zh: 在功利主义伦理的无灵魂状态所造成的哲学缺口处，走来了来自当时仍然落后、盛行虔信主义的德国的内省型启蒙思想家（Aufklärer）。从康德到黑格尔的德国“古典哲学家”的目标，不是像西方哲人常常希望的那样粉碎宗教，而是把科学的新理性主义与旧日灵性的世俗化版本以及宗教的内向性综合起来。因此在德国，启蒙运动的抱负是借助科学清除基督教中的迷信，以便更好地通过把基督教的道德真理改铸为理性术语来保存它们。他们劳动的成果是一种“纯粹理性界限内的宗教”的哲学——用康德的表述——这种解决方案最终掏空了启示宗教，并把人类理性神化。因此，正是德国哲学赋予了启蒙运动的人观以最崇高、最令人陶醉的表达，而这种表达也通过马克思最直接地哺育了十九世纪的社会主义。
en: Into the philosophical breach created by the soulessness of utilitarian ethics stepped the inward-looking
, the enlighteners, of still backward and pietistic Germany. The aim of the German “classical philosophers” from Kant to Hegel was not to crush religion, as the Western

so often wished, but to synthesize the new rationalism of science with a secularized version of the old spirituality and the inwardness of religion. In Germany the aspiration of the Enlightenment therefore was to purge Christianity of superstition with the aid of science, the better to preserve its moral verities by recasting them in rational terms. The fruit of their labors was a philosophy of “religion within the bounds of reason alone,” in Kant’s formulation—a solution that wound up eviscerating revealed religion and divinizing human reason. Thus it is German philosophy that gave the Enlightenment view of man its most exalted and intoxicating expression, which is also the expression that, through Marx, fed most directly into nineteenth-century socialism.

zh: 康德朝这一目标迈出了关键一步：他把基督教伦理重新表述为理性“普遍而必然”法则的“命令”，唯有这种法则才能“无条件地”发出命令。于是，在“实践”意义上，传统的金律变成了理性法则：“无论对自己还是对他人，都要永远把人当作目的，绝不仅仅当作手段。”每个人都配享这种绝对尊重，因为每个人都是“纯粹理性”的所在，因此，即使在一个世俗世界里，每个人仍必须被当作“仿佛”拥有不朽灵魂来对待。基于这种神圣的理性，康德呼应卢梭，赞扬“普通人”是未来“世界公民”地位的受益者，他相信这种可能性正在法国革命中实现。
en: Kant took the crucial step towards this end when he reformulated Christian ethics as “imperatives” of the “universal and necessary” laws of reason, which alone can command “categorically.” Thus in “practical” terms the traditional Golden Rule became the rational law: “Act so as to treat man, in your own person as well as in that of any one else, always as an end, never merely as a means.” Each man merited this absolute respect because each was the seat of “pure reason,” and so, even in a secular world, each must still be treated “as if” he possessed an immortal soul. And on the basis of this sacral rationality, Kant, echoing Rousseau, extolled the “common man” as the beneficiary of a future “world citizenship,” a possibility he believed was being realized in the French Revolution.

zh: 黑格尔把基督教转化为哲学的工作大大推进了一步，他把二者融合为一个螺旋上升的辩证过程，在其中，人类理性的发展也是上帝自我意识的发生。
这种自我意识也是自由，因为理解使我们摆脱对外在法则盲目服从的必然性。因此，“世界历史是自由意识的进步”
，而人的理性灵魂是一种精神，它在时间中展开和成长，走向越来越高的自我意识和自由。
en: Hegel took the transformation of Christianity into philosophy a great step further by fusing the two into a spiralling dialectical process, in which the development of human reason was also the emerging self-consciousness of God.
This self-consciousness was also liberty, since understanding frees us from the necessity of blind submission to external law. Thus “World History is progress of the consciousness of freedom,”
and the rational soul of man is a Spirit that unfolds and grows over time towards ever greater self-consciousness and liberty.

zh: 具体说来，“自由意识的各种等级”如下：“东方人只知道一个人是自由的，希腊人和罗马人知道一些人是自由的，而我们[现代人]知道一切人本身、也就是作为人，都是绝对自由的。”此外，“这种[对自由的]认识最初是在宗教中、在精神最内在的领域中产生的。”因此，对黑格尔来说，现代公民的自由源于灵魂的个体不朽。由于这一概念对古代世界相当陌生（关于古代民主的其他局限，稍后还会谈到），奴隶制对柏拉图和亚里士多德来说并不是丑闻。但一旦灵魂不朽的概念被世俗化并成为一种社会规范，它便不可避免地成为现代欧洲人心目中的丑闻。
en: Concretely, the “various grades in the consciousness of freedom” are these: “the Orientals knew that only
was free, the Greeks and Romans knew that
are free, while we [moderns] know that

men, absolutely, that is, as men, are free.” Moreover, “this realization [of freedom] first arose in religion, in the innermost region of spirit.” Thus for Hegel the freedom of the modern citizen has its origin in the individual immortality of the soul. Since this concept was quite foreign to the ancient world (and more will be said shortly about other limitations of ancient democracy), slavery was not a scandal to Plato and Aristotle. But it inevitably became one to the modern European mind once the concept of the immortal soul had been secularized and made into a social norm.

zh: 尽管黑格尔没有描述世俗化的实际过程（他所说的“自我意识”的增长正是指此），但不难勾勒其轮廓。在整个基督教中世纪，社会不平等并未被视为与每个灵魂的不朽价值相矛盾，因为不平等被认为是原罪的后果。
堕落如此败坏了人性，以致多数人从属于少数人，既是社会凝聚、乃至生存所必需，也是最终得救所必需的涤罪过程。因此，个体不朽的果实只会在来世到来，并取决于灵魂如何在此生度过种种危险。当然，正是这种观点，被追随费尔巴哈的马克思称为“颠倒的”意识，并被马克思视为“使人非人化”。
en: Although Hegel did not delineate the actual process of secularization (which is what he meant by the growth of “self-consciousness”), it is not difficult to suggest its outline. Throughout the Christian Middle Ages social inequality was not perceived as contradicting the immortal worth of each and every soul because inequality was considered to be a consequence of original sin.

The Fall had so corrupted human nature that the subordination of the many to the few was required both for the cohesion, indeed survival, of society, and as a purgative necessity for eventual salvation. Thus the fruits of individual immortality would come only in the next world, and in accordance with the way the soul had navigated the perils of life in this one. And it is this view, of course, that Marx, following Feuerbach, called an “inverted” consciousness and that he found “dehumanizing.”

zh: 到十八世纪中叶，关于理性万能的新乐观主义削弱了原罪学说乃至一般神学对人心的控制，这无疑是那些年平等主义革命的主要原因之一。再次是卢梭标志了决定性的转变：他宣称，恶以及随之而来的不平等进入世界，并非由于人性中某种天生的缺陷，而是由于社会的缺陷构造，其现存秩序建立在强者对弱者的篡夺性统治之上。因此，恶的起源是社会性的，而非人固有的；于是，人的自然善性将允许废除一切不平等。正如黑格尔所论，基督教灵魂由此转化为世俗公民。
en: By the mid-eighteenth century the new optimism about the omnipotence of reason had weakened the hold of the doctrine of original sin, and of theology generally, over men’s minds, and this was certainly one of the main causes of the egalitarian revolution of those years. Again, it was Rousseau who marked the decisive shift by declaring that evil, and with it inequality, came into the world not through some innate flaw of human nature, but through the defective constitution of society, whose existing order was founded on the usurped lordship of the strong over the weak. Evil was thus social in origin, not intrinsic to man; men’s natural goodness, therefore, would permit the abolition of all inequality. And so, as Hegel argued, the Christian soul was transformed into the secular citizen.

zh: 如果我们以为这段对形而上学和神学的离题论述与苏联社会主义的起源无关，那就大错特错了。因为马克思在把黑格尔重新正立过来时，头脑中仍然保留着这位大师的形而上学。正如莱谢克·科拉科夫斯基在《马克思主义主流》开篇所说：“卡尔·马克思是一位德国哲学家。”
en: If we should think that this excursus into metaphysics and theology is irrelevant to the genesis of Soviet socialism, we would be quite wrong. For Marx, in standing Hegel on his feet, still preserved the master’s metaphysics in his own head. As Leszek Kolakowski put it in the opening sentence of
, “Karl Marx was a German philosopher.”

zh: 这种带有近乎神化的人之观念的德国哲学，只有转化为政治，才能成为现代世界的一支主要力量；马克思正是通过把它嫁接到法国革命所开启的平等主义传统上而做到了这一点。关于这一传统的意义，最伟大的评论者是托克维尔。
en: This German philosophy, with its quasi-divinized idea of man, could become a major force in the modern world only if it were translated into politics; and this Marx did by grafting it onto the egalitarian tradition that came out of the French Revolution. On the import of that tradition the great commentator is Tocqueville.

zh: 尽管遭遇种种暂时的挫败，1789年开启的革命仍然开创了当代政治宇宙。它的后果勾勒出现代性的核心问题：从自由放任经济的管理，到大众社会的政治安排，再到为所有人促进社会正义。这一后果也给了我们现代政治话语的词汇：自由主义、保守主义、民族主义、社会主义，以及其他许多带有当时新后缀“主义”的词，都在1789年之后的三十来年里出现。
而在这些新词中，有一个古老的术语——民主——如今获得了一系列新的含义。
en: The year 1789, for all its temporary failures, inaugurated the contemporary political universe. Its fallout delineated the central problems of modernity, from the management of a laissez-faire economy to the political ordering of a mass society to the fostering of social justice for all. This fallout also gave us the vocabulary of modern political discourse: Liberalism, conservatism, nationalism, socialism, and a host of other words with the then new suffix “ism” all appeared in the thirty-odd years after 1789.
And among these neologisms was an ancient term—democracy—which now acquired a new range of meanings.

zh: 如前所述，从柏拉图到美国建国之父，“民主”一直带有暴民统治和无政府的负面含义。尽管我们如今轻率地谈论“杰斐逊式民主”，但杰斐逊本人并不使用这个词，他只偶尔谈到“人民政府”，而他的新政党被称为“共和党”。“民主”在美国开始以正面意义使用，只是在1820年代和1830年代，当时普选首次成为一个原则问题；在法国则是在1830年代和1840年代，原因相同。尽管如此，民主在这两个国家都迟迟未进入官方修辞；在美国，杰克逊和林肯都没有使用它——尽管在非政府层面，沃尔特·惠特曼用过它，而且用的是抒情的民粹主义语调；在美国和法国，直到世纪末，具有魔力的术语仍然是“共和”。（当然，在宪政但仍实行君主制的英国，“民主”和“共和”都只为无足轻重的边缘群体所使用。）民主只是在第一次世界大战期间才获得其目前的威力和含义范围，当时伍德罗·威尔逊用它把法国和英国此前狭隘的民族斗争——对抗“专制”德国——转变为一场在全世界争取人民政府的道德政治十字军东征。
en: As already noted, from Plato to America’s Founding Fathers, “democracy” had carried the negative charge of mob-rule and anarchy. Although we now speak blithely of “Jeffersonian democracy,” the term was not used by Jefferson himself, who only occasionally spoke of “popular government” and whose new party was called the “Republican Party.” “Democracy” began to be employed in a positive sense in America only in the 1820s and 1830s when universal suffrage first became an issue of principle, and in France in the 1830s and 1840s for the same reason. Still, democracy was slow to enter official rhetoric in either country; In America, neither Jackson nor Lincoln used it—although at a nongovernmental level Walt Whitman did, and in lyrical populist tones; in both America and France until the end of the century the magic term remained “republic.” (And in constitutional but monarchical Britain, of course, both “democracy” and “republic” were the property of an insignificant fringe.) Democracy acquired its present potency and range of meanings only during the First World War, when Woodrow Wilson used it to transform the hitherto narrowly national struggles of France and Britain against “autocratic” Germany into a moral-political crusade for popular government everywhere.

zh: 在这个复兴的希腊标签的多种含义中，与本书目的最相关的是托克维尔《论美国的民主》所传达的那种含义。他指的并不是美国宪政，而是美国的平等主义。他把平等主义视为一个雅努斯双面的现象。他在1830年代写作，当时这个词的负面含义正让位于与普选相关的正面内涵，因此他的民主概念是一种混合体，交织着不祥的预感与期待。作为一位深受1789年革命经验影响的法国人，他确信平等主义的拉平力量是现代世界一切政治的首要动力。与此同时，他深感忧虑：这股不可抗拒的力量可能与自由不相容——那些自由主要源于贵族，曾在旧制度下被孟德斯鸠颂扬，当时则由复辟欧洲的阶级宪政政府保障，而自由—寡头的英国是其伟大典范。
en: Among the multiple meanings of this revived Hellenic label, the most relevant for our purposes is the one conveyed by Tocqueville’s

. By this he meant not American constitutionalism but egalitarianism in America. And he saw egalitarianism as a Janus-headed phenomenon. Writing as he did in the 1830s when the negative meaning of the term was giving way to the positive connotations associated with universal suffrage, his concept of democracy was a hybrid mingling foreboding and anticipation. As a Frenchman coming out of the experience of 1789, he was convinced that the leveling force of egalitarianism was the prime mover of politics everywhere in the modern world. At the same time, he was deeply concerned that this irresistible force might be incompatible with the liberties, largely of aristocratic origin, which had been celebrated under the Old Regime by Montesquieu and which were then guaranteed by the class-based constitutional governments of Restoration Europe, for which liberal-oligarchic Britain was the great model.

zh: 由于“民主”一词是希腊语的，我们往往以为它今天的含义与公元前五世纪雅典的含义相同，以为伯里克利的葬礼演说就是我们自身政治传统的源头。
同样，我们以为“共和”一词是拉丁语的，因而从西塞罗到麦迪逊和孔多塞，它的含义也有连续性。但这只有非常有限的一部分是真实的。现代政治与希腊—罗马过去的共同之处，确实在于一部分人口通过民选官员和立法议会参与公共事务。这种“政治”——这个词本身显然来自希腊语
——在二十世纪之前不存在于任何非欧洲社会。但现代政治拥有而其古代前身完全陌生的东西，是人的至高尊严、每一个个体的神圣性的观念。这一价值来自刚刚讨论过的现代西方的文化转变。古代政体中没有“权利法案”或“人权宣言”，公民身份的概念不是建立在仅仅作为人这一事实上，而是建立在世袭或法律授予的、属于某一特定城邦或共和国（
）的某一阶级的成员资格上。因此，本雅明·贡斯当在复辟时期捍卫自由主义时，可以区分“古代人的自由与现代人的自由”：前者指少数人参与公共事务的自由，后者指所有人不受社会干涉、作为主权个体生活的自由。
en: Since the term “democracy” is Greek, we tend to assume that it means the same thing today as it did in the Athens of the fifth century B.C., and that Pericles’s Funeral Oration is the source of our own political tradition.

Similarly, we assume that since the word “republic” is Roman, it too has a continuity of meaning, from Cicero to Madison and Condorcet. But this is only very partially true. What modern politics does have in common with the Greco-Roman past is the participation of a part of the population in public affairs through elective officers and legislative assemblies. This kind of “politics”—the word itself is obviously from the Greek

—existed in no non-European societies until the twentieth century. But what modern politics possesses, and what is quite alien to its ancient predecessor, is the idea of the supreme dignity of man, the sanctity of each and every individual. This value emerged from the cultural transformations of the modern West just discussed. There were no “bills of rights” or “declarations of the rights of man” in ancient polities, and the concept of citizenship was grounded not in the mere fact of being human but in hereditary or legally granted membership in one or another class of a given polis or

. Thus Benjamin Constant, defending liberalism under the Restoration, could draw a distinction between “ancient and modern freedom,” wherein the former meant the freedom of the few to participate in public affairs and the latter meant the freedom of all to be left alone by society in order to live as sovereign individuals.

zh: 因此，希腊民主意味着把自由民中最低等级的“民众”（

）纳入公共事务，这是为了整个城邦的健康所必需的措施，而不是一种自然权利。此外，这个“民众”是作为一个群体、与更高的社会群体并列参与政治的——有点类似于欧洲旧制度中的等级——而不是与高于自己的等级处于平等地位，更不是以“一人一票”为基础。罗马共和国更加寡头化，平民完全处于主要政治回路之外。前面已经指出，所有古代政体都把奴隶——他们占人口的相当大一部分——完全排除在公民身份之外。诚然，各种现代共和国曾一度允许奴隶制；但由于这些共和国同时也宣告了“不可剥夺的人权”，这一反常现象只能导致危机并最终废除。而较为温和的政治歧视形式，即有财产资格限制的选举权，则更容易消亡。但古代世界没有废奴主义，普选也从未被考虑过。
en: Accordingly, Greek democracy meant inclusion of the lowest order of free men, the
, in public affairs as a measure necessary for the health of the polis as a whole, not as a natural right. Moreover, this

participated in politics as a group alongside higher social groups—somewhat along the lines of an estate in the European Old Regime—not on a footing of equality with its superiors, still less on the basis of “one man one vote.” The Roman republic was even more oligarchic, with the plebs quite outside the main political circuit. And it has already been noted that all ancient polities completely excluded slaves, who represented sizable portions of their populations, from citizenship. To be sure, various modern republics for a time permitted slavery; but since these republics also proclaimed the “unalienable rights of man,” this anomaly could only lead to crisis and eventual abolition. And the milder form of political discrimination, a suffrage based on property, perished even more easily. But there was no abolitionism in the ancient world, and universal suffrage was never even contemplated.

zh: 正是由于这种独特的现代共和国概念，现代民主在其不断左倾的运动中，越来越超出宪政政府和法治，走向主权在民和普遍平等。因此，对托克维尔来说，民主意味着“条件的平等”（
，即把法国和整个欧洲旧制度所特有的、法律上的等级或阶层的社会阶梯全部拉平。但他想到的不只是旧制度，因为革命后的世界也有自己的不平等阶梯。这些阶梯建立在财富赋予的地位和权力之上，体现为“阶级”制度——用的是1830年代和1840年代的新称谓。
这些新的不平等形式，以及未来一切可能的不平等形式，也将受到现代性那种内在而不可抗拒的逻辑——即平等——的挑战。回想托克维尔的表述：“难道可以相信，民主在推翻贵族和国王之后，会在资产阶级和富人面前止步吗？”
en: It is because of this distinctively modern concept of the republic that modern democracy, in its steadily leftward movement, reached increasingly beyond constitutional government and the rule of law toward popular sovereignty and universal equality. Thus, for Tocqueville, democracy meant “

the leveling of all the social gradations of the legal hierarchy of estates, or orders, that characterized the Old Regime in France and throughout Europe. But he did not have only the Old Regime in mind, for the post-Revolutionary world had its own gradations of inequality. Based on the status and power conferred by wealth, these gradations were embodied in a system of “classes,” to use the new designation of the 1830s and 1840s.

These new forms of inequality, as well as all future possible ones, would also be challenged by which immanent, implacable logic of modernity that was equality. To recall Tocqueville’s formulation: “Can it be believed that democracy, after having overthrown aristocracy and the kings, will stop short before the bourgeoisie and the rich?”

zh: 正是在这种民主动力中，蕴含着那个被1830年代另一个新词“社会主义”所指称的伟大运动的起源。因为，如果对作为平等的民主观念进行毫不留情的逻辑推演，就不可避免地会得出社会主义的概念。只要社会中存在财富差异，就会有权力和地位的差异；只要存在权力和地位的差异，就会有一部分人对另一部分人的剥削，以及一些人对另一些人的支配。而任何剥削和从属都是对人类尊严的否定，是对人的神圣人格的亵渎。因此，不平等就是非人化，因而是一种道德丑闻；如果世界要真正文明化，就必须终结这种丑闻。
en: It is in this democratic impetus that lies the origin of that great movement designated by another neologism of the 1830s—“social-ism.” For, if one is ruthlessly logical about the idea of democracy as equality, then one inevitably arrives at the concept of socialism. So long as there are differences of wealth in society, there will be differences of power and status; and so long as there are differences in power and status, there will be exploitation of some men by others, and domination of some human beings by other human beings. But any exploitation and subordination are a denial of human dignity, a profanation of the sacred persona of Man. Inequality, therefore, is dehumanization, and thus a moral scandal that must be ended if the world is to become truly civilized.

zh: 做到这一点的手段是对个人财富的社会占有，而这正是完整社会主义的核心工具性纲领。正如马克思在《共产党宣言》中所说：“共产党人的理论可以用一句话概括：消灭私有制。”
由此可知，私有制的果实——利润——以及实现这种利润的手段——市场——也必须被消灭。至此，社会主义的最大化公式就完整了：社会主义起源于一个道德观念——平等——并完成于一个实践纲领——终结私有制和市场。任何不及此者，都算不上完整或充分的社会主义。
en: The means to do this is the social appropriation of individual wealth, and this is the core instrumental program of integral socialism. As Marx put it in
“The theory of the Communists may be summed up in the single phrase: Abolition of private property.”

From this it follows that the fruit of private property—profit—and the means for realizing this profit—the market—must also be abolished. With this, the maximalist formula of socialism is complete: Socialism originates in a moral idea—equality—and culminates in a practical program—the end of private property and the market. Anything short of this is something less than full or integral socialism.

zh: 但这个作为完全非资本主义的社会主义最大化纲领，历来被证明不经过一场具有巨大破坏性的革命就无法实施。因此在实践中，社会主义运动通常满足于较为温和的目标和进化式的方法。当然，正是这一点导致了前面已经提到的各种纲领——从累进税制到普遍福利国家——它们也声称拥有“社会主义”的头衔，并极大地混淆了关于其“真正”含义的争论。然而，本书不必陷入这种混乱。在这里，“社会主义”始终带有其完全非资本主义的最大化含义。因为这是马克思所意图的形式，也是1917年的剧烈动荡的局势使社会主义在俄国得以采取的形式。
en: But this maximalist program of socialism as full noncapitalism has always proved impossible to implement without a shattering revolution. So in practice the socialist movement has usually settled for more modest goals and for evolutionary methods. And it is this, of course, that has led to the already-noted gamut of programs—from progressive taxation to a universal welfare state—that also claim the title “socialist” and that have so confused the debate about its “true” meaning. No such confusion, however, need intrude into the present book. Here “socialism” will always carry its maximal meaning of full noncapitalism. For this was the form intended by Marx and that the shattering circumstances of 1917 permitted socialism to take in Russia.

zh: 在整个十九世纪，社会主义一直是一个道德观念、一个反对和抗议的运动。只有到布尔什维克的十月，社会主义才跨过从运动到社会的门槛。也只有到那时，民主力量才得以检验这样一个命题：废除私有制和市场将产生平等的道德世界和人的充分人道化。而这件事的裁决直到我们自己的世纪之交才明确作出。因此，在此之前，共产党人的完整社会主义是所有西方次等社会主义的金本位；而结果是，后者在政治上越是民主、越倾向渐进变革，它们实现的社会主义经济纲领就越少。因此，它们长期既被苏联人大胆的成果所震慑，又被其残暴的方法所困扰。苏联社会主义由于捷足先登，在1989—1991年的大崩溃之前一直界定着社会主义话语。
en: Throughout the nineteenth century, socialism had been a moral idea, a movement of opposition and protest. It was only with the Bolshevik October that socialism crossed the threshold from movement to society. It was only then that democratic forces were able to test the proposition that abolition of private property and the market would produce the moral world of equality and the full humanization of man. And the verdict in this matter was not clearly rendered until our own fin-de-siècle. So until then, the integral socialism of the Communists was the gold standard for all the lesser breeds of socialism in the West, and it turned out that the more these latter were democratic and evolutionary politically, the less they realized of the socialist economic program. They were therefore chronically as overawed by the Soviets’ bold results as they were disturbed by their brutal methods. Soviet socialism, by getting there first, thus defined the socialist discourse until the great crash of 1989-1991.

zh: 马克思与阶级斗争
en: MARX AND CLASS STRUGGLE

zh: 通常的假设无疑是，社会主义观念在现代世界中之所以发挥这种关键作用，是因为它是“无产阶级”（1830年代和1840年代的又一个新词）的阶级意识。但事实远非如此。工业革命和新工人阶级的中心是英国，而初生社会主义意识形态的故乡是革命后的法国，更确切地说，是1830—1848年七月王朝时期的法国。诚然，罗伯特·欧文早在1827年就使用了形容词名词“社会主义者”，但英国主要的激进运动是宪章运动，它只主张议会改革和普选。正是在法国，形形色色的社会主义者和共产主义者站在期待下一次革命爆发的左派前列；也正是在法国，1831年，圣西门主义者皮埃尔·勒鲁的笔下，对“社会”的新关切首次获得了总体化的后缀“主义”。
en: The usual assumption no doubt is that the socialist idea played this pivotal role in the modern world because it was the class consciousness of the “proletariat” (another neologism of the 1830s and 1840s). But this was hardly the case. The center of the industrial revolution and the new working class was Britain, whereas the homeland of nascent socialist ideology was post-Revolutionary France, or more precisely, France during the July Monarchy of 1830-1848. It is true that Robert Owen used the adjectival noun “socialist” as early as 1827, but the main English radical movement was Chartism, which stood simply for parliamentary reform and universal suffrage. It was in France that socialists and communists of various stripes were at the forefront of a Left awaiting the next revolutionary outbreak; and it was in France, under the pen of the Saint-Simonian Pierre Leroux, in 1831, that the new concern for the “social” first acquired the totalizing suffix “ism.”

zh: 然而，认为社会主义是工业工人的阶级意识这一信念，在七月王朝时期已经盛行。马克思和恩格斯提供了最著名的表达。在恩格斯后来附在《宣言》一个译本后的脚注中，他指出，他和马克思把英国视为“资产阶级”经济发展的“典型”，把法国视为其政治发展的典型。
但他没有指出的是，从英国工业化推导出法国革命，或从1840年代英国工人阶级的状况推断法国社会主义后来的政治，都是不合逻辑的推论。
这一切意味着，社会主义的动力不在经济状况中，而在政治状况中——法国的情况戏剧性地表明了这一点——而这些政治状况远比任何一个阶级的意识更为广阔。
en: Yet the belief that socialism is the class consciousness of industrial workers was already prevalent during the July Monarchy. The most notable expression of this is given by Marx and Engels. In a footnote that Engels later appended to a translation of
, he remarked that he and Marx had taken England as “typical” of the economic development of the “bourgeoisie,” and France as typical of its political development.

But what he did not note was that it is a non sequitur to derive the French Revolution from English industrialization, or to deduce the later politics of French socialism from the condition of the English working class in the 1840s.

All of which means that the socialist impetus will be found not in economic circumstances but in political circumstances, as dramatized by the French case, and that these political circumstances are far broader than the consciousness of any one class.

zh: 正如托克维尔所指出的，一旦旧制度的等级阶梯被拉平，新制度的阶级阶梯在逻辑上也岌岌可危。因此，早在1796年，就出现了第一个现代拉平运动——格拉古·巴贝夫的“平等派密谋”。这当然被镇压了，其遗产一直潜藏到1830年七月革命。但这次推翻的结果是，“公民国王”路易-菲利普的新“资产阶级君主制”被平等主义情绪和另一次起义的期待所撕裂——那次起义将最终完成1789年未竟的事业，而这一事业在1830年只是过于怯懦地被重新拾起。因此，复兴的左派生活在对1789年第二次降临的期待中，期待一个新共和国，这一次不仅是政治的，也是社会的。正是在这种炽热的气氛中，“社会主义”开始流行；“共产主义”作为其最激进的平等主义形式出现，延续着巴贝夫的传统；
而“民主”获得了那种拉平的含义，正是这种含义促发了托克维尔对现代世界政治社会学的思考。
en: As Tocqueville noted, once the old-regime hierarchy of estates was levelled, the new-regime hierarchy of classes was also logically imperiled. Thus as early as 1796 there appeared the first modern movement of levelling, the

of Gracchus Babeuf. This, of course, was put down, and its heritage remained submerged until the July Revolution of 1830. But the result of this overturn was that the new “bourgeois monarchy” of the “citizen king,” Louis Philippe, was riven by egalitarian sentiments and expectation of another insurrection, one that would at last complete the unfinished work of 1789, which had been too timidly resumed in 1830. So the revived Left lived in anticipation of a Second Coming of 1789, and of a New Republic that, this time, would be not merely political but social as well. It is in this perfervid atmosphere that “socialism” became current; that “communism” emerged as its most radically egalitarian form, continuing in the tradition of Babeuf;
and that “democracy” acquired that levelling connotation which prompted Tocqueville’s reflections on the political sociology of the modern world.

zh: 这种沸腾的情绪很快在1848年革命中溢出，也促发了马克思和恩格斯对现代性更为精细的思考。正如他们常说的，他们的体系——首次完整地汇集在1845年的《德意志意识形态》中——是英国政治经济学、法国革命社会主义和德国古典哲学的融合。对于由此产生的混合物，他们给了当时最激进的标签：共产主义；并在1848年的《宣言》中以通俗的、口号式的形式阐述了他们的学说。尽管当时几乎无人知晓，他们和他们的理论注定在世纪末获得非凡的命运。之所以如此，是因为尽管他们在法国和英国度过了多年，他们仍然是德国哲学家。对于英国和法国为民主现代性所作的那些平淡而直率的贡献，他们附加了德国思辨传统的核心特征：其逻辑力量和富于远见的想象力、其宏大的历史视野，以及其对人的隐秘神化。正是凭借这一综合，他们的运动——在那个时代所有相互竞争的社会主义派别中（他们轻蔑地给这些派别贴上“乌托邦”的标签）——将在现代激进主义的角逐中成为世界历史的赢家。
en: This ebullition, which was soon to overflow in the Revolution of 1848, also prompted the more elaborate reflections on modernity of Marx and Engels. As they often put it, their system, first fully brought together in the

of 1845, was a fusion of British political economy, French revolutionary socialism, and German classical philosophy. To the resultant amalgam they gave the most radical label of the day, communism, and they set forth their doctrine in popular, sloganlike form in the

of 1848. Though almost unknown at the time, they and their theory were fated to have a phenomenal destiny by the end of the century. And this was so because, for all their years in France and England, they remained German philosophers. To the prosaic and forthright British and French contributions to democratic modernity, they adjoined cardinal features of the German speculative tradition: its logical and visionary power, its grand historical sweep, and its covert divination of Man. It is with this synthesis that their movement, among all of the competing socialist sects of that age (to which they derisively affixed the label “utopian”), would emerge as the world-historical winner in the sweepstakes of modern radicalism.

zh: 既然我们知道马克思和恩格斯将会获胜，最好在这里、在1840年代的背景和他们默默无闻的时期讨论其体系的性质，而不是在后面、在他们世纪末胜利的背景中讨论。也就是说，最好在马克思主义最接近黑格尔和哲学的时候来看它，而不是在其后来伪实证主义和自称接近达尔文的外衣下看它。
en: Since we know that Marx and Engels are going to win, it is best to discuss the nature of their system here, in the context of the 1840s and the period of their obscurity, rather than later, in the context of their fin-de-siècle triumph. That is, it is best to look at Marxism at its closest to Hegel and to philosophy, rather than in its later guise of pseudopositivism and would-be closeness to Darwin.

zh: 必须从两个层面接近这个体系：其正式信条的层面和其深层结构的层面。正式信条是最明显、最广为人知的。简言之，它们是：第一，一种社会学，其中经济和社会基础决定社会的文化、政治和意识形态上层建筑；第二，一种历史理论，其中人类在阶级斗争的驱动下，从奴隶制社会、封建社会、资产阶级社会前进，走向其“史前史”在社会主义中的终结；第三，一种经济学理论，阐述资本主义的“内部矛盾”，这些矛盾最终将产生无产阶级的社会主义革命。
en: The system must be approached at two levels: that of its formal tenets and that of its deep structures. The formal tenets are the most obvious and the best known. In brief, these are: first, a sociology in which the economic and social base determines the cultural, political, and ideological superstructure of society; second, a theory of history in which mankind, driven by the class struggle, progresses from slave-holding, to feudal, to bourgeois society, towards the end of its “pre-history” in socialism; third, a theory of economics setting forth the “internal contradictions” of capitalism that would at last produce the socialist revolution of the proletariat.

zh: 经济学理论的正式信条是十九世纪马克思主义最突出的方面，它们确实以不可抗拒的逻辑展开。这一理论从一切价值都由人类劳动创造的原则出发，追踪劳动者的“剩余价值”被攫取以产生“资本积累”的无情过程。这些资本随后被投入节省劳动的机器，这既代表着生产力的巨大进步和人类的财富，也代表着“资产阶级生产方式”终结的开始。因为竞争产生了“利润率下降规律”，这同时导致资本越来越集中在少数人手中，以及无产阶级的“日益贫困化”。由此产生的生产资料集中和通过工厂制度实现的劳动社会化，“最终达到一个与资本主义外壳不相容的地步。外壳被炸得粉碎。资本主义私有制的丧钟敲响了。剥夺者被剥夺。”社会主义于是从废墟中产生。
en: The formal tenets of the economic theory were the most prominent aspect of Marxism in the nineteenth century, and they indeed unfold with an implacable logic. Beginning with the principle that all value is created by human labor, this theory traces the inexorable process whereby the “surplus value” of the laborer is confiscated to produce the “accumulation of capital.” This capital is then invested in laborsaving machinery, which represents both a great advance of productivity and riches for the species and the beginning of the end for the “bourgeois mode of production.” For competition generates the “law of the falling rate of profit,” and this produces simultaneously the concentration of capital in fewer and fewer hands and the “increasing immiseration” of the proletariat. The resulting centralization of the means of production and the socialization of labor through the factory system “at last reach a point where they become incompatible with their capitalist integument. The integument is burst asunder. The knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.” And socialism emerges from the ruins.

zh: 这整个体系——社会学、历史理论、经济学——看起来是对发达工业社会的分析，其本意也确实如此。简言之，马克思主义的方法表面上似乎是欧洲最发达地区所特有的，而这些地区的文明被视为历史的顶点，因而也是所有较落后国家在达到社会主义之前必须经历的不可回避的阶段。马克思明确说过，欧洲向世界其余部分展示了它们的未来。
en: This entire system—the sociology, the theory of history, the economics—looks like, and indeed was intended to be, an analysis of advanced industrial society. In short, the method of Marxism appears on the surface to be specific to the most developed portions of Europe, whose civilization was viewed as the culmination of history and thus the unavoidable stage through which all more backward countries would have to pass before reaching socialism. And Marx explicitly said that Europe showed to the rest of the world its future.

zh: 马克思主义所预期的社会主义革命当然没有首先发生在西欧。但这与其说使马克思主义失效，不如说指向其正式信条背后的深层结构。因为这一深层结构适用于世界任何地方的情况，甚至包括大体上仍处于工业化之前的社会；即使在马克思所论证的资本主义特定内部矛盾早已不再令人信服很久之后，它仍然适用。这一深层结构由矛盾原则本身——辩证法——所界定；对黑格尔和马克思来说，辩证法都是驱动历史逻辑的动力。而这种力量通过一切存在者永恒不断的异化和重生过程来运作。
en: The socialist revolution anticipated by Marxism of course did not occur first in Western Europe. Yet this does not so much invalidate Marxism as point to the deep structure behind its formal tenets. For this deep structure is relevant to conditions anywhere in the world, even in largely preindustrial societies, and in times long after the specific internal contradictions of capitalism argued by Marx have ceased to be plausible. This deep structure is defined by the principle of contradiction itself—the dialectic—which for Hegel and Marx both was the motive force driving the logic of history. And this force operated by a perpetual process of alienation and rebirth of all being.

zh: 黑格尔对这一愿景的表述如下：用抽象的逻辑术语说，辩证法是宇宙戏剧，其中一切不完善的存在形式都通过失去、或异化自身、从属于自身之外某物的行为而超越自身。用神学术语说——异化最初是一个神学概念——道成肉身是上帝的自我异化，同理也是人被提升到不朽。在自然领域，神圣理性把自己客观化，屈从于物质世界，以便显现整个自然的理性法则。在人类历史中，较为原始的文化形式和民族必须衰亡，被更高的文化和民族摧毁，以完善整体的人类生活：因此希腊必须让位于罗马，罗马必须让位于蛮族，才能产生更高的基督教文明、并最终产生现代西方的自由主义文明。
en: Hegel’s presentation of this vision runs as follows: In abstract logical terms, the dialectic is a cosmic drama in which all imperfect forms of being transcend themselves through the act of losing, or alienating, themselves by subordination to something outside themselves. In theological terms—and alienation was initially a theological concept—the Incarnation is the self-alienation of God, and by the same token, the raising up of man to immortality. In the natural realm, divine reason objectifies itself in servitude to the material world in order to make manifest the rational laws of all nature. And in human history, more primitive cultural forms and nations must decay and be destroyed by higher ones in order to perfect the life of mankind as a whole: So Greece had to give way to Rome, and Rome to the barbarians in order to produce the still higher Christian, and ultimately liberal, civilization of the modern West.

zh: 因此，进步处处只有通过否定、剥夺和死亡才得以实现。所以，异化既具破坏性又具创造性，既使人屈辱又使人高贵，既奴役人又解放人：一句话，它是自我丰富的。因此，黑格尔式的理性回溯到古老的宗教观念：失去灵魂者将寻得灵魂，救赎只有通过罪、苦难和匮乏才能到来。或者，用黑格尔在主人与奴隶的形而上学寓言中更世俗的说法：主人通过奴役奴隶来肯定自我，但这种肯定是不完善的，且没有意识到自己的同一性；而奴隶在为主人劳动时改造了物质世界，并凭借其创造力上升到更真实的自我；当这种自我意识与主人的自由相结合时，奴隶便成为人类的普遍意识。
en: Thus, everywhere progress comes about only through negation, privation, and death. Alienation, therefore, is both destructive and creative, humiliating and ennobling, enslaving and liberating: In a word, it is self-enriching. Thus, Hegelian Reason harks back to the old religious notion that he who loses his soul shall find it, and that redemption comes only through sin, suffering, and privation. Or as Hegel put the matter in more secular terms in the metaphysical parable of the master and the slave: The master affirms his selfhood imperfectly and without awareness of his identity by subjugating the slave; but the slave, in laboring for the master, transforms the material world and by his creativity rises to a more genuine selfhood; and when to this self-consciousness is adjoined the freedom of the master, the slave becomes the universal consciousness of Man.

zh: 对马克思来说，通过主奴辩证法进行的自我丰富异化过程，表现为阶级斗争；我们应当记得这一原则对他的思想有多么核心：“一切历史，”正如《宣言》第一页所宣告的，“都是阶级斗争的历史。”这一点值得强调，因为阶级斗争将成为苏联人马克思主义学说的核心条款。还必须强调，这场斗争不是黑格尔那种心灵和灵魂的斗争，而是暴力的、物质的斗争。马克思从弗朗索瓦·基佐和其他研究法国大革命的历史学家那里借来“阶级斗争”（
）的概念，把宗教—哲学辩证法转化为阶级战争。
en: For Marx, the process of self-enriching alienation through the master-slave dialectic comes out as the class struggle; and we should recall how central this principle is to his thought: “All history,” as the first page of the

proclaims, “has been the history of class struggles.” The matter bears emphasis because the class struggle would become the cardinal article of Marxist doctrine for the Soviets. And it must be emphasized also that this struggle is not a struggle of minds and souls, as with Hegel, but a violent, physical struggle. Taking the concept of the “
” from François Guizot and other French historians of the Great Revolution, Marx transformed the religious-philosophical dialectic into class warfare.

zh: 阶级斗争由一些人对另一些人的残酷而必要的剥削所驱动；只有通过这种非人化，人才能最终成为完整的人。因此，一个阶级的劳动被异化来服务于另一个阶级，以便为人类的整体进步创造物质手段。与此同时，阶级对这种剥削的怨恨产生了推动人类从一种生产方式前进到另一种生产方式的社会革命。于是，历史无情地从古代平民与贵族的斗争，推进到中世纪农奴与封建领主的斗争，再到现代无产阶级与资产阶级的“最后斗争”（
en: The class struggle is fueled by the cruel but necessary exploitation of some men by others; only through such dehumanization can man at last become fully Man. Thus the labor of one class is alienated to serve another class in order to create the material means for the overall progress of the species. At the same time, class resentment of this exploitation produces social revolutions propelling humanity forward from one mode of production to another. And so history implacably advances from the struggle of plebians against patricians in antiquity to that of serfs against feudal lords in the Middle Ages, on to
of the proletariat against the bourgeoisie in the modern age.

zh: 因此，对马克思来说，人类进步戏剧的最后、最伟大的主角是无产阶级。

但这个无产阶级并不简单地是某位英国政治经济学家可能定义的那个“工人阶级”。马克思的无产阶级，毋宁说类似于黑格尔所说的理性官僚制的“普遍阶级”，这个群体的使命是在国家政府中成为绝对哲学的载体。马克思用无产阶级——一个“来自下方的普遍阶级”——取代了可以说是“来自上方的普遍阶级”；无产阶级的使命是使一个建立在阶级不平等所造成的非人化之上的社会重新获得人性，而它之所以能完成这一转变，恰恰因为它是国家之下资产阶级市民社会中最受非人化的阶级。因此，无产阶级是救赎的阶级，因为它是生产的阶级，同时又是受苦的阶级。
en: Thus, for Marx the last and greatest protagonist of the drama of human progress is the proletariat.

But this proletariat is not simply the “working class” as that group might be defined by some British political economist. Marx’s proletariat, rather, is an analogue of what Hegel called the “universal class” of rational bureaucracy, a group whose mission was to be the vehicle of Absolute philosophy in the government of the State. Marx replaces what might be called this “universal class from above” with the proletariat, a “universal class from below” and the proletariat’s mission is to humanize a society founded on the dehumanization of class inequality, a transformation it can accomplish precisely because it is the most dehumanized class in bourgeois civil society under the State. The proletariat is thus the redeemer class because it is the productive and yet the suffering class.

zh: 正如马克思本人在1843年所说——那时他还没有在工厂的工作台旁亲眼见过真正的无产者：
en: As Marx himself put it in 1843, before he had ever laid eyes on real proletarians at a factory bench:

children: 必须形成一个被彻底的锁链束缚的阶级，一个市民社会中的阶级，但这个阶级并不是市民社会的一个阶级，一个使一切阶级解体的阶级，一个因苦难具有普遍性而具有普遍性质的社会领域；它不要求任何特殊的补救，因为加在它身上的不是特殊的冤屈，而是一般的冤屈……最后，一个若不从一切其他社会领域中解放自身、因而若不解放一切其他社会领域就不能解放自身的阶级；总之，一个完全丧失人性的阶级，只能通过人类的完全救赎来救赎自身。这个作为特殊阶级的社会解消，就是无产阶级。

zh: 在这个救赎方案中，落后的德国——正因其落后，它是一个被剥夺、被压迫的无产阶级民族——对青年马克思来说具有特殊使命。“这种解放只有在实践中采取这样一种理论观点才有可能：即人是人的最高本质。德国若不从对中世纪的局部胜利中解放出来[即从单纯的自由主义中解放出来]，就不能从‘中世纪’中解放出来。在德国，不摧毁一切奴役，就不能摧毁任何一种奴役……德国的解放就是人的解放。”这段话以一句惊人的论断结束：“哲学是这种解放的头脑，无产阶级是它的心脏。哲学只有通过无产阶级的废除[扬弃，
]才能实现，无产阶级只有通过哲学的实现才能被废除。”
换言之，对马克思来说，无产阶级与其说是一个社会群体，不如说是一个形而上学实体，其本质由匮乏给定，而其被剥夺同时又是废除一切匮乏所必需的宇宙力量的来源。

if one adopts the point of view of that theory according to which man is the highest being for man. Germany will not be able to emancipate itself from the
unless it emancipates itself from the partial victories over the Middle Ages [that is, from mere liberalism]. In Germany
type of enslavement can be abolished unless
slavery is destroyed…. The
