In other words, for Marx the proletariat is less a social group than a metaphysical entity whose essence is given by privation, and whose deprivation is at the same time the source of the cosmic strength necessary to abolish all privation.

zh: 马克思主义的这一范式或核心概念，显然又一次以世俗术语回应了基督教的一个核心概念。我们在这里看到的是经典宗教逻辑的重演：在末日，最后者将成为最先者，卑微者将被抬高；但它被赋予了一种新的战斗性、甚至报复性的色彩。这是“温顺者和精神贫乏者有福了，因为他们将继承大地”的逻辑，只是温顺者如今被召唤去壮大和丰富自己的精神，以便在阶级斗争中作战。
en: This paradigm or core concept of Marxism obviously echoes in secular terms (once again) one of the core concepts of Christianity. What we have here is a reprise of the classic religious logic that in the final days the last shall be first and the humble shall be exalted, but it is given a new militant, indeed vengeful cast. It is the logic of “blessed are the meek and poor in spirit, for they shall inherit the earth,” but with the meek now summoned to fortify and enrich their spirit to do battle in the class struggle.

zh: 这一范式也可以从欧洲先进工业国家的工人阶级，转移到任何其他被剥夺、被羞辱、被伤害、被剥削或受害的群体。列宁可以把它应用于“落后”俄国的“工农联盟”。同样，马克思在1843年赋予“中世纪”德国的无产阶级民族角色，列宁在1917年可以把它转给“资本主义链条中最薄弱的环节”——“半殖民地”俄国。或者，在第二次世界大战之后，这一范式可以转移到由前殖民地和不发达国家组成的第三世界，如弗朗茨·法农和菲德尔·卡斯特罗的思想，或毛泽东和胡志明的政治。或者，在二十世纪后期的过度发达美国，这一范式可以从阶级迁移到种族、性别、性取向。被剥削者的“普遍阶级”的本质，确实似乎在其普遍性中永恒不变。
en: This paradigm may also be transferred from the working class of the advanced industrial nations of Europe to any other group that is deprived, humiliated, offended, exploited, or victimized. It could be applied by Lenin to a “worker and peasant alliance” in “backward” Russia. Similarly, the role of proletarian nation that Marx in 1843 had assigned to “medieval” Germany could in 1917 be transferred by Lenin to the “weakest link in the capitalist chain,” “semicolonial” Russia. Or, after the Second World War, the paradigm could devolve to the Third World of excolonial and underdeveloped nations, as in the thought of Frantz Fanon and Fidel Castro, or in the politics of Mao Tse-tung and Ho Chi Minh. Or, in the overdeveloped America of the late twentieth century, the paradigm could migrate from class, to race, to gender, to sexual orientation. The essence of the “universal class” of the exploited indeed seems eternal in its universality.

zh: 因为它的普遍性建立在卢梭所推崇的“怜悯”能力之上，即对那些受苦或被剥夺者的同情感受，而这种“怜悯”既是社会主义的情感基础，也是其道德基础。它也与康德承认从卢梭那里获得的“对人性的尊重”和“对普通人的尊重”相同，康德把这一点置于其伦理体系的核心。而这种富有同情心的平等主义政治，始终对知识分子的“贵族义务”（
）意识具有特殊吸引力。但像雅努斯一样，它也可能逐渐变成对主人的吞噬性仇恨。因此，马克思的历史贡献在于赋予平等追求一种愤怒的、充满斗争性的冲力——这种冲力只有在法国革命之后才可能出现，并且是即将到来的解放斗争——社会主义的“最后斗争”——取得胜利所必需的。
en: For its universality rests on the faculty of what Rousseau extolled as “pity,” or compassionate feeling, for those who are suffering or deprived, and this “pity” is both the emotional and the moral basis of. socialism. It is also the same as that “respect for human nature” and the “common man” that Kant acknowledged he derived from Rousseau and that he put at the heart of his ethical system. And the politics of compassionate egalitarianism has always had a special appeal to the sense of

among intellectuals. But, Janus-like, it could also shade off into a consuming hatred of the master. Thus, the historical contribution of Marx was to give the quest for equality a wrathful and agonistic thrust, one possible only after the French Revolution and necessary for the success of the coming emancipatory struggle—
of socialism.

zh: 高度资本主义与世纪末
en: HIGH CAPITALISM AND FIN DE SIÈCLE

zh: 马克思主义的这一核心范式或深层结构，在创始人的早期著作中最为明显，当时他们仍接近黑格尔，并生活在对后来成为1848年革命的期待中。但从1867年的《资本论》开始，语调更像是对政治经济学的科学批判；1883年马克思去世后，由恩格斯独自掌舵，运动的语调变得越来越实证主义：作为德国哲学家的马克思，让位于“社会科学的达尔文”马克思——恩格斯在其战友墓前如此说。而正是在这种自命科学的外衣下，马克思主义最终成为一支世界历史力量。
en: This core paradigm, or deep structure, of Marxism is most apparent in the early works of the founders, when they were still close to Hegel and living in expectation of what became the Revolution of 1848. But beginning with

in 1867, the tone is more like that of a scientific critique of political economy, and after Marx’s death in 1883, with Engels alone in charge, the tone of the movement became increasingly positivistic: Marx the German philosopher gave way to Marx “the Darwin of the social sciences,” as Engels put it at his comrade’s graveside. And it is in this would-be scientific guise that Marxism at last became a world-historical force.

zh: 把马克思主义从默默无闻推向显赫的是1871年的巴黎公社。这一由普法战争产生的偶然事件，与马克思博士的国际工人协会（第一国际）毫无关系。但欧洲各国政府看到一个大都城被红色起义占领的景象，惊恐万分，把爆发归咎于马克思的组织——这个“荣誉”他求之不得。而把马克思主义推上顶峰的，是1891年俾斯麦反社会主义法的废除；该法在巴黎公社之后几年通过，目的是把革命的幽灵挡在德意志帝国之外。这使马克思主义者有可能夺取欧洲最大的工人阶级政党，从而最终主导第二国际。第二国际于1889年在法国大革命一百周年之际成立于巴黎，既是为了完成大革命的任务，也是为了继承公社的事业。
en: What catapulted Marxism out of obscurity and into prominence was the Paris Commune of 1871. This fortuitous event, produced by the Franco-Prussian War, was one with which Dr. Marx’s International Working Men’s Association, or the First International, had nothing to do. But the established governments of Europe, horrified at the spectacle of a major capital taken over by Red insurrection, blamed Marx’s organization for the outbreak—an “honor” he was only too glad to accept. And what put Marxism over the top was the repeal, in 1891, of Bismarck’s Anti-Socialist Laws, which had been passed a few years after the Paris Commune to keep the specter of revolution out of Imperial Germany. This made it possible for Marxists to capture the largest working-class party in Europe, and thus eventually to dominate the Second International, which was founded in Paris in 1889 on the hundredth anniversary of the French Revolution, both to complete its task and to continue that of the Commune.

children: 〔译注〕原书此处写1891年；德国反社会党人法于1890年9月30日到期失效。
〔译注〕原书此处写1891年；德国反社会党人法于1890年9月30日到期失效。

zh: 然而，社会主义运动日益增长的成功也带来了倒退到温和路线的危险。但马克思主义已经准备好了解药。马克思在1848年为其《宣言》采用了左派最激进的标签；他从来不喜欢同年首次听到的另一个术语——“社会民主”——所包含的改革主义含义。然而，1863年后新的德国工人党使他无法摆脱这个术语。因此，为了对抗该党的改革主义倾向，他在1875年的《哥达纲领批判》中（1891年才由恩格斯出版）重新使用共产主义一词，并把它规定为社会主义的更高、最终阶段，届时“社会将在自己的旗帜上写下：各尽所能，按需分配。”这种从历史终点处的社会主义产生共产主义的两阶段愿景，将被列宁和苏联人继承，同时也为二十世纪区分独裁社会主义者与民主社会主义者提供了标签。但应当强调，在这一术语精细化的整个过程中，集体主义左派的基本、通称始终是社会主义。
en: The growing success of the socialist movement, however, also carried the danger of backsliding into moderation. Yet Marxism was ready with an antidote. Marx had adopted the most radical label on the Left for his

in 1848; he never liked the reformist implications of another term first heard in that year—“social democracy.” Still, he was stuck with it by the new German workers’ party after 1863. So, to combat this party’s reformist tendencies, in the “Critique of the Gotha Program” of 1875 (published only in 1891 by Engels), he returned to the term communism and made it the higher, final stage of socialism, when “society [would] inscribe on its banner: From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs.” The two-stage vision of communism arising from socialism at the end of history would be continued by Lenin and the Soviets, while at the same time furnishing the labels separating dictatorial from democratic socialists in the twentieth century. Yet it should be emphasized that throughout this process of terminological refinement the basic and generic term for the collectivist Left always remained socialism.

zh: 但第二国际以及马克思主义在其中的成长，如果没有在十九世纪最后几十年达到顶点的深刻经济和社会变化，是不可能的。因为这一时期正是阿诺德·汤因比在1895年所称的“工业革命”的成熟期。今天的历史学家会把它追溯到十八世纪后期的英国，以及使机器生产成为可能的最初几项发明——从珍妮纺纱机到蒸汽机。到十八世纪末，工厂制度已在第一个“现代”工业——纺织业——中取代了家庭作坊制度。到1820年代，蒸汽机被搬上铁轨，产生了铁路；这种运输的现代化很快又要求把采煤和冶铁结合起来，形成第三项伟大的工业事业——钢铁冶金。因此，到1848年前夕，早期工业主义的工厂—矿山—烟囱经济已在英国充分出现；其顶峰通常被认为是1851年的水晶宫博览会，同一年，英格兰和威尔士约一半人口首次居住在城市。
en: But the growth of the Second International, and of Marxism within it, would have been impossible without the profound economic and social changes that culminated during the last decades of the nineteenth century. For this was the period of the maturity of what Arnold Toynbee, in 1895, called the “industrial revolution.” Historians today would trace its beginnings to late eighteenth-century Britain and to the first inventions—from the spinning Jenny to the steam engine—that made possible machine production. By the end of that century the factory system had replaced the domestic system of cottage manufacture in the first “modern” industry, textiles. By the 1820s the steam engine had been put on rails to produce the railroad, and this modernization of transport soon necessitated bringing together the mining of coal and the smelting of iron into a third great industrial endeavor, steel metallurgy. Thus by the eve of 1848, the mill-mine-and-smokestack economy of early industrialism had fully emerged in Britain; its apotheosis is usually taken to be the Crystal Palace Exhibition of 1851, the same year in which, for the first time, about half the population of England and Wales lived in towns.

children: 〔译注〕原书将汤因比使用“工业革命”一词的时间写作1895年；阿诺德·汤因比于1883年逝世，其《工业革命讲演录》初版于1884年。
〔译注〕原书将汤因比使用“工业革命”一词的时间写作1895年；阿诺德·汤因比于1883年逝世，其《工业革命讲演录》初版于1884年。

zh: 到1820年代，新的工业秩序已到达比利时；在1830年代和1840年代资产阶级君主制时期，它到达法国。在这种推动下，早期社会主义思想家圣西门创造了“工业主义”一词，用以指称新的社会经济组织体系。当然，初生社会主义所关心的正是这个新工业世界的种种弊病；“贫困化”（
）一词与“无产阶级”并列，用以指称新秩序中受屈辱和受伤害的人。显然，马克思正是从这种早期工业主义的世界中，得出了其体系中非形而上学、即经验性的部分，并预见到工业无产阶级在德国的出现。
en: By the 1820s the new industrial order had reached Belgium; and in the 1830s and 1840s, during the Bourgeois Monarchy, it reached France. Under this impetus, the protosocialist Saint-Simon coined the term “industrialism” to designate the new system of socioeconomic organization. It was, of course, with the evils of this new industrial world that nascent socialism was concerned, and the term “pauperism” took its place alongside “proletariat” to designate the humiliated and the offended of the new order. It is obviously from this world of early industrialism that Marx derived the nonmetaphysical, or empirical, parts of his system, in anticipation of the industrial proletariat’s appearance in Germany.

zh: 这最终随着1860年代德国的“起飞”而实现，时间大致与美国内战后工业化的巨大浪潮同时。到1880年代，整个西欧和北美终于存在一个真正的工业社会。在这个世界里，最初在1840年代提出的“贫困化”问题，成为那个时代的中心社会问题。因为新的大众工人的处境确实糟透了。此外，由于欧洲人口中越来越大的比例集中在大城市，与较富裕阶级的对比变得触目惊心地明显。在英国，迪斯雷利谈到“两个民族”，马克思把“劳动阶级”称为“危险阶级”；而巴黎公社则既展示了苦难，也展示了新的城市和工业秩序所产生的爆炸性潜力。
en: This finally occurred with the German “takeoff” of the 1860s, at roughly the same time as the great American post-Civil War surge of industrialization. By the 1880s there at last existed a genuine industrial society throughout Western Europe and North America. In this world the issue of “pauperism,” first posed in the 1840s, became the central social issue of the age. For the condition of the new mass of workers was indeed abysmal. Moreover, the contrast with the more affluent classes was made shockingly visible by the concentration of an ever-larger proportion of Europe’s population in great cities. In England, Disraeli spoke of “two nations” and Marx called the “laborious classes” the “dangerous classes,” while the Paris Commune demonstrated both the misery and the explosive potential generated by the new urban and industrial order.

zh: 历史学家一直在争论解放现代工业普罗米修斯对人造成的代价。从长远看，它当然改善了先进国家大多数人的物质处境。但从短期看，这些代价显然巨大。诚然，前工业欧洲的乡村生活往往贫困得令人煎熬；直到“饥饿的四十年代”，饥荒仍很频繁，迁往城市或漂洋过海到美国，长期是最受剥夺者的主要出路。尽管如此，新工业城镇的生活往往也难说有所改善：住房简陋，卫生条件骇人，劳动艰苦且报酬低微。此外，工厂工人失去了工匠或自耕农的独立性，沦为资本控制的巨大机器上的一个齿轮。而且，工人阶级当时大多尚未组织工会，没有罢工权，也没有任何社会保障“安全网”。因此，到世纪末，无产阶级确实是社会中最受剥夺、最被排斥、最受害的群体。
en: Historians have debated the human costs of unbinding the modern industrial Prometheus. In the long run, it certainly improved the material lot of most of the population in the advanced countries. But in the short run, these costs were clearly great. To be sure, life in the villages of preindustrial Europe had often been a grindingly penurious one; famine was frequent as late as the “hungry forties” and migration to the cities or across the ocean to America was long the chief remedy for the most deprived. Still, life in the new industrial towns often was hardly an improvement: Housing was primitive, sanitary conditions were appalling, and labor was arduous and poorly remunerated. In addition, the factory worker had lost the independence of the artisan or peasant freeholder and become a mere cog in a vast machine controlled by capital. Moreover, the working class was as yet largely ununionized, without the right to strike, and without any social-security “safety net.” By the fin de siècle, the proletariat thus was indeed the most deprived, excluded, and victimized group in society.

zh: 因此，它组织起来、发出声音、在政党中找到表达的权利，处于民主政治的最前沿；而由于到世纪末这个群体约占城市人口的三分之一，“劳工问题”变得越来越紧迫。相应地，第二国际把五一节定为国际劳工的节日，并于1892年采用《国际歌》作为其颂歌，以取代那首曾经革命、如今却“资产阶级共和主义的”赞歌《马赛曲》。
en: Accordingly, its right to organize, to be heard, and to find expression in political parties was therefore at the cutting edge of democratic politics; and since by the end of the century this group represented about one-third of the urban population, the “labor question” became an ever more pressing one. The Second International, accordingly, made May Day the international feast of labor, and in 1892 it adopted the “Internationale” as its hymn to replace the once revolutionary but now “bourgeois republican” anthem “The Marseillaise.”

zh: 第二国际从成熟的工业体系和不断壮大的工人阶级中汲取力量，远比第一国际更配得上自己的名称。到1905年，全国性的社会主义政党也已在英国、法国、奥地利和较小的欧洲国家出现；甚至美国也有某种社会主义运动。诚然，在西方世界任何地方，社会主义者都远未成为多数（他们得票最高的是1912年的德国，获得三分之一选票）；更谈不上有任何社会主义者上台执政的前景。古典自由主义、自立自强的个人主义、自由放任经济学和宪政民主在整个西方世界仍占绝对优势。尽管如此，马克思的“共产主义幽灵”在1848年还不过是一个吓唬人的东西，如今却已成为相当实在的事物；而他的学说因德国社会民主党的成功而声望大增，并以这种或那种形式被国际的所有分支所采纳，从法国的让·饶勒斯到俄国的格奥尔基·普列汉诺夫。
en: Drawing strength from a mature industrial system and a growing working class, the Second International merited its name far more than the First. By 1905, nationwide socialist parties had also appeared in Britain, France, Austria, and the lesser European states; even the United States had something of a socialist movement. To be sure, nowhere in the Western world were socialists near to being a majority (their highest tally was in Germany in 1912, when they polled one-third of the vote); still less was there any prospect of socialists coming to power. Classical liberalism, rugged individualism, laissez-faire economics, and constitutional democracy were still very much in the ascendancy throughout the Western world. Nonetheless, Marx’s “specter of Communism,” which in 1848 had been little more than a bogeyman, was now a fairly substantial affair, And his doctrine, made prestigious by the success of German Social Democracy, was in one or another form taken up in all branches of the International, from that of Jean Jaurès in France to that of Georgii Plekhanov in Russia.

zh: 正是第二国际这种实证主义的、以工人为中心的（
）马克思主义，将在俄国被改造，最终产生世界上第一场马克思主义革命。在这一时期，凸显出来的是经济和社会学信条，即学说的正式特征。因此，马克思主义政党的重点在于历史的不可抗拒逻辑：欧洲将逐阶段地从封建社会走向资产阶级社会，再走向社会主义社会。但那种更为浪漫、形而上学和革命的深层结构——自我超越的异化——从未远离表面，而危机会把它激发出来。
en: It is the positivistic and

Marxism of the Second International that would be adapted in Russia to produce, at last, the world’s first Marxist revolution. In this period it is the economic and sociological tenets, the formal features of the doctrine, that came to the fore. The emphasis of Marxist parties, therefore, was on the implacable logic of history leading Europe, stage by stage, from feudal, to bourgeois, to socialist society. But the more romantic, metaphysical, and revolutionary deep structure of self-transcending alienation was never far below the surface, and crisis would bring it out.

zh: 因此，马克思主义拥有一种独特的制胜品质组合：这个体系的天才之处，在于把一种伪救赎宗教表达为自命为实证的科学，并把此前专属于来世的慰藉与此世中作为人类最高智力成就的科学知识的确定性结合起来。正如阿兰·贝桑松所说：“摩西和圣约翰……知道他们相信……[马克思和]列宁相信他们知道。”
en: Thus Marxism came to possess a unique winning combination of qualities: The genius of the system is to express a pseudosalvation religion as a would-be positive science, and to combine the consolations hitherto reserved for the next world with the certitude of scientific knowledge that is man’s supreme intellectual achievement in this one. As Alain Besançon put it: “Moses and Saint John … knew that they believed…. [Marx and] Lenin believed that they knew.”

zh: 马克思主义的威力，还因这一学说与一个比社会主义更模糊、更庞大的术语——左派——相联系而得到加强；这个术语能够把非社会主义者带入理性与进步的道德共同体。

把政治世界分为左派和右派两个阵营，当然始于法国大革命及其各议会中激进派与温和派的座次安排；到复辟时期，这种二分法已或多或少成为另外两个新标签——“自由派”和“保守派”——的同义词。这一分野源于政治活跃且意识形态化的法国，到1830年代已向东传播到德国，而那里尚未真正存在政治，于是它只被应用于意识形态，如“左派黑格尔主义者”这样的术语。在这种扩展意义上，这种二分法传遍欧洲，最后才进入政治更为渐进和务实的国家：它在十九世纪末到达英国，在二十世纪初到达美国，从而使两国已有的自由—保守、民主—共和分野激进化。
en: The potency of Marxism is reinforced by the doctrine’s association with a vaguer and vaster term than socialism, one capable of bringing nonsocialists into the moral fellowship of reason and progress—the Left.

The division of the political world into two camps, the Left and the Right, dates of course from the French Revolution and the seating arrangements of radicals and moderates in its various assemblies; by the time of the Restoration, this bifurcation had become more or less synonymous with two other new labels, “liberals” and “conservatives.” From its origins in France, where politics were dynamic and ideological, the division by the 1830s had spread eastward to Germany, where politics did not yet exist, and where it was applied to ideology alone, as in such a term as “Left Hegelian.” In this extended meaning the dichotomy spread throughout Europe, coming into use last in countries where politics were more gradualistic and pragmatic: It reached Britain towards the end of the nineteenth century and the United States at the beginning of the twentieth, thereby radicalizing their existing Liberal-Conservative and Democratic-Republican divides.

zh: 这种二分法的命运是，其内容随时间不断向左移动。起初，“左派”意味着反对传统王权，至少主张君主立宪，或在其更激进的边缘主张以普选为基础的民主共和国；它还意味着敌视国教。“右派”则被动地捍卫“祭坛与王座”，后来又主张以财产资格限制选举权作为防线、抵御民主。此外，由于1789、1830和1848年接连的革命冲击把历史本身推向左边，左派也被称为“运动党”，而右派则被称为“抵抗党”。最后，1848年使“人民”成为左派的先锋，从而突出了这样一种观念：政治共和国还不够，真正的解放需要社会共和国，即“社会民主”。于是，社会主义在左派的左翼找到了自己的位置。
en: The destiny of this dichotomy was that its content shifted constantly to the Left over time. At the beginning, the “Left” meant opposition to traditional kingship in favor of, at the least, a constitutional monarchy, or, on its more radical fringe, a democratic republic founded on universal suffrage; it also meant hostility towards established religion. The “Right” stood reactively for defense of “altar and throne,” and later for holding the line against democracy at a property suffrage. Moreover, since the successive revolutionary shocks of 1789, 1830, and 1848 were pushing history itself to the Left, the latter camp also came to be known as the “party of movement,” whereas the Right became known as the “party of resistance.” Eighteen forty-eight, finally, made the “people” the spearhead of the Left, thereby bringing to the fore the notion that the political republic was not enough, and that a social republic, or “social democracy,” was necessary for true human emancipation. And so socialism found its place on the left of the Left.

zh: 1848年还给了这个社会主义左派一个伟大的象征：红旗。这面旗帜在旧制度下曾被用作要求骚乱人群解散、宣告即将镇压的信号。但它的含义在1791年第二个巴士底日被颠倒过来：当时“两个世界的英雄”拉法耶特举起它，以流血手段镇压一场激进抗议；于是，骚乱的象征被反抗者接过，转变为解放革命的象征。尽管红旗在1848年被第二共和国拒绝，但它仍被保留下来，以备左派中较温和的成分一旦动摇或失败时使用。从此，这面旗帜将与波旁王朝的白旗并列——后者自1814年复辟伴随的贵族恐怖以来，一直是反革命的象征。
en: The year 1848 also gave this socialist Left its great symbol, the Red Flag. This banner had been used under the Old Regime as a means of reading the riot act and heralding the repression of civil disorder. But the flag’s meaning was reversed on the second Bastille Day, in 1791, when the “hero of two worlds,” Lafayette, raised it to put down in blood a radical protest; the symbol of seditions riot was taken up in defiance and transformed into that of liberating revolution. Although the Red Flag was rejected by the Second Republic in 1848, it remained in reserve should the softer elements of the Left ever falter or fail. And this banner would henceforth be juxtaposed with the White Flag of the Bourbons, the symbol of counterrevolution since the aristocratic terror that accompanied the Restoration in 1814.

zh: 因此，社会主义理想继续推动左派向左，直到世纪末。而恰恰在世纪末，这场运动又获得了两个新的层面：国际主义与争取和平的斗争。
en: Thus the socialist ideal continued to drive the Left leftward until the end of the century. And at the very fin de siècle, the movement acquired two new overlays: internationalism and the struggle for peace.

zh: 1789年之后的一个世纪里，左派一直是爱国的，事实上还以革命解放战争为荣；这些情感在1848年“各民族之春”中达到顶点，直到1871年仍激励着巴黎公社社员。但这种民族主义的出现，只是以“一人一票”为基础的民主的逻辑对应物。因为一旦国王的所有臣民都成为平等公民，一个统一的集团或大众就产生了，王国便让位于由公意驱动的民族。但普选在逻辑上也意味着普遍兵役制——这也是现代战争通常远比早期战争血腥的原因之一，另一个原因是科学和技术的发展。
en: For a century after 1789, the Left had been patriotic and, indeed, had gloried in wars of revolutionary liberation; these sentiments, culminating in the “Springtime of the Peoples” of 1848, had still inspired the Parisian Communards as late as 1871. But the emergence of this nationalism was only the logical counterpart of democracy founded on “one man one vote.” For once all the king’s subjects have become equal citizens, a uniform bloc or mass is created, and kingdoms give way to nations animated by a general will. But universal suffrage also logically entails universal military service—which is one reason, along with the development of science and technology, why modern wars have generally been far bloodier than earlier ones.

zh: 到世纪之交，欧洲大部分地区已组织成拥有大规模征兵军队的紧凑民族国家。因此，工人—士兵的社会主义倡导者成为国际主义者，并在他们的新颂歌中宣告“明天，国际将成为全人类”。与此同时，昔日祭坛与王座的捍卫者在新民族中发现了社会秩序的堡垒，转而成为爱国者、甚至沙文主义者，列阵反对“那些没有祖国的人”——德皇威廉二世如此称呼他的工人征召兵。于是，民族主义——如今常常与新的政治反犹主义结合——从左派迁移到右派，马志尼和密茨凯维奇的抒情让位于特赖奇克和巴雷斯的刺耳声调。
en: At the century’s close, most of Europe was organized into compact nation-states with mass conscript armies. Thus the socialist advocates of the worker-soldier became internationalists, and in their new hymn proclaimed that “tomorrow the International would be the human race.” Concurrently, the former defenders of altar-and-throne discovered in the new nation a bulwark of social order and turned into patriots, even chauvinists, arrayed against “those fellows without a fatherland,” as Kaiser Wilhelm II called his worker-conscripts. And so nationalism—now often combined with a new political anti-Semitism—migrated from Left to Right, and the lyricism of Mazzini and Mickiewicz gave way to the strident tones of Treitschke and Barrès.

zh: 这种转变伴随着世界上第一个和平运动的出现。从启蒙运动开始，圣皮埃尔神父和康德（在贵格会等宗教和平主义者之后）这样具有远见的思想家就设想过“永久和平”的方案。但总体而言，由各民族组成的欧洲与由国王组成的欧洲一样，认为战争是高尚的。直到1914年前的紧张积累时期，对和平的关切才成为一项群众事业，社会主义国际才成为其主要代言人。因此，当欧洲列强在贪婪和虚荣的驱动下争夺瓜分非洲和亚洲时，经济“帝国主义”被自由派和社会主义者一致谴责为战争的根源，因而被视为一支对立的国际力量。
en: This shift was accompanied by the emergence of the world’s first peace movement. Beginning with the Enlightenment, visionaries like the Abbé de Saint-Pierre and Kant (in the wake of such religious pacifists as the Quakers) had imagined schemes for “perpetual peace.” But on the whole the Europe of peoples found war as noble as had the Europe of kings. It was only in the buildup to 1914 that concern for peace became a mass cause, and that the Socialist International emerged as its principal voice. So as the European powers, driven by both greed and vainglory, scrambled to partition Africa and Asia, economic “imperialism” was denounced as the cause of war by liberals and socialists alike, and thus viewed as a rival international force.

zh: 因此，到1914年前夕，左派是一个由民粹主义、和平主义和国际主义力量组成、通常具有世俗性质的松散实体，其重心越来越倾向于内部的社会主义左翼。而维系这个联盟、同时赋予社会主义其中道德优势的动力，是对右派的恐惧和反动的威胁。“左派没有敌人”成为进步政治的黄金法则，而“帮了右派的忙”则是对进步事业的重大背叛。到第一次世界大战时，这种国际主义政治文化将为布尔什维克的国内外命运提供不可或缺的母体。
en: And so, by the eve of 1914, the Left was a diffuse entity of populist, pacifist, internationalist, and usually secular forces increasingly weighted toward its internal, socialist left. And the dynamic that held this coalition together, while at the same time giving socialism the moral edge within it, was fear of the Right and the threat of reaction. “No enemies to the Left” became the golden rule of progressive politics, and “playing into the hands of the Right” the great betrayal of the cause of progress. By the First World War, this internationalist political culture would furnish the indispensable matrix for both the domestic and foreign fortunes of Bolshevism.

zh: 但是，在十九世纪关于社会的论述中，概念链条上缺失的一环——即社会主义应当取代的“资本主义”——在哪里呢？事实是，直到将近世纪末，人们根本不谈资本主义；而当他们开始使用这个术语时，主动权并非来自“资本家”本身，而是来自试图给他们希望否定的世界打上烙印的社会主义者。
en: But where, in the nineteenth-century discourse on society, is the missing link in the conceptual chain—namely, the “capitalism” that socialism is supposed to replace? The fact is that until almost the end of the century people did not talk about capitalism at all; and when they did take up the term, the initiative came not from the “capitalists” themselves, but from socialists seeking to brand the world they hoped to negate.

zh: 在亚当·斯密、大卫·李嘉图、让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊、约翰·斯图亚特·密尔，或古典政治经济学的任何其他名家中，都找不到“资本主义”一词。事实上，甚至在卡尔·马克思那里也找不到这个词。“资本”一词自十六世纪以来一直用来指货币和物质生产资料。“资本家”（
）一词出现在狄德罗的《百科全书》中，指资本所有者或企业家。但到1830年前后，“资本”已开始指金钱的社会权力，或作为一种政治力量的“金钱利益”。当然，这正是马克思所接过的用法，并将其普遍化为“资本主义生产方式”。他也谈到“资产阶级社会”（
），并把“我们的时代”称为“资产阶级的时代”（这里用的是法语词，比德语
更明显地是一个社会经济术语）。
但他从未跃向名词化的“主义”；如同所有这类词一样，这一后缀的作用是把事物实体化为一个总体系统，把经济、社会、政治和文化领域融合为一个具有自身内在“逻辑”的整体。
en: One will search in vain for the word capitalism in Adam Smith, David Ricardo, Jean-Baptiste Say, John Stuart Mill, or any of the other worthies of classical political economy. Indeed, one will not even find the word in Karl Marx. The term “capital” had been in use since the sixteenth century to signify the monetary and material means of production. The word “capitaliste” appears in the

of Diderot to designate the owner of capital, or an entrepreneur. But by around 1830, “capital” had come to mean the social power of money, or the “monied interest” as a political force. And this, of course, is the usage that Marx picked up and generalized into the “capitalist mode of production.” He also spoke of “bourgeois society” (
) and called “our epoch” the “epoch of the bourgeoisie” (this time using the French word, more clearly a socioeconomic term than the German

But he never made the leap to the substantive “ism,” which, as with all such words, has the effect of hypostatizing matters into a total system, fusing the economic, the social, the political, and the cultural realms into a single whole endowed with its own inherent “logic.”

zh: 名词化的“资本主义”最早由路易·勃朗等社会主义者在1840年代使用，而且只是偶尔使用，且仅带贬义，指一种为资本所有者服务的制度。正是带着这个含义，它在大约1870年由卡尔·冯·罗德贝尔图斯和卡尔·李卜克内西等人物推向更广泛的流通。它接下来从德国传播的地方，并非我们可能预料的英国，而是俄国——在1877年革命组织“土地与自由”的纲领中。
事实上，以农民为导向的俄国社会主义者已经表明，他们比整个工业西方更早熟：1872年，他们就让马克思的《资本论》有了第一个外文译本。这一切再次表明，社会主义和革命的冲动最初源于道德和政治考虑，而非经济考虑。
en: The substantive “capitalism” was first, and only occasionally, used by such socialists as Louis Blanc in the 1840s, and then only in the pejorative sense of a system working for the owners of capital. It was with this meaning that it was put into broader circulation around 1870 by such figures as Karl von Rodbertus and Karl Liebknecht. From Germany, it next made its way not to England, as we might expect, but to Russia in the 1877 program of the revolutionary organization “Land and Freedom.”
Indeed, Russian peasant-oriented socialists had already shown themselves to be more precocious than the entire industrial West by giving Marx’s

its first translation into a foreign language in 1872. All of which serves to show, once again, that the socialist and revolutionary impulse derives initially from moral and political, rather than economic, considerations.

zh: “资本主义”真正作为一个总体系统出现，只能追溯到1890年代。这是在德国社会民主党的兴起，以及德国经济学中英国分析进路的拥护者与本土历史学派之间“方法之争”（
）的共同影响下发生的。在这场争论中，后者接过了社会主义者古老的论战口号，并赋予它庞大的结构内容和发展内容；结果是，到1900年，无论对德国自由派还是社会主义者来说，现代性都被定义为“资本主义”，即一个无所不包的系统。

于是，维尔纳·桑巴特在1902年出版了《现代资本主义》，马克斯·韦伯在1904年出版了《新教伦理与资本主义精神》。（然而，列宁得益于俄国激进主义早熟，已抢先一步，在西伯利亚写成、于1899年出版了《俄国资本主义的发展》。）因此，正是可追溯到康德和黑格尔、如今转而回应社会民主党挑战的德国总体综合传统，产生了十九世纪最后一个伟大的“主义”。历史更先进却在概念上落后的法国人、英国人和美国人，直到1917年之后才完全接受这一术语。
en: The real emergence of “capitalism” to designate a total system dates only from the 1890s. This occurred under the combined influence of the rise of German Social Democracy and of the

(methodological debate) in German economics between the adherents of the British analytical approach and those of the native historical school. In this debate the latter took up the socialists’ old polemical slogan and gave it massive structural and developmental content, with the result that by 1900, for both German liberals and socialists, modernity came to be defined as “capitalism” in the sense of an all-encompassing system.
Thus Werner Sombart produced his
in 1902, and Max Weber his

children: Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism

children: The Development of Capitalism in Russia

en: , which he composed in Siberia and published in 1899.) Thus it is the German tradition of global synthesis, going back to Kant and Hegel, and now turned to answering the challenge of Social Democracy, that produced the last of the great nineteenth-century “isms.” The historically more advanced yet conceptually laggard French, British, and Americans would not fully naturalize this terminology until after 1917.

zh: 然而，一旦这个新词成为西方文化领域的通用货币，它究竟意味着什么？“资本主义”显然比“社会主义”意味得更多，因为它指的是在它出现之前就已真实存在的制度。尽管如此，它并不指称任何可以严格定义、并在历史上清晰划界的东西。因此，像社会主义一样，它远更多的是一个形而上学而非经验性的术语。也像社会主义一样，它的含义从伦理领域延伸到制度领域，有时还把两者结合并混淆起来。在道德上，它带有活力充沛的正面含义，但更强烈地带有个人贪婪和社会剥削的负面含义。在制度上，它从十九世纪曼彻斯特自由主义的极端自由放任政策——其批评者所谓的“野蛮”或“未驯服的资本主义”——一直延伸到二十世纪服务于福利国家的各种国家管制模式。在历史上，它涵盖各种发展程度，从十六、十七世纪的商业和“买办”资本主义，到古典工业体系，再到后工业的服务业主导经济。在社会学上，在二十世纪内部，它从美国以自由市场为主的经济，延伸到欧洲共同体更多干预主义和“社会市场”的经济，再到日本的国家—工业社团主义。
en: Yet what did this neologism mean once it had become the coin of the Western cultural realm? “Capitalism” clearly means quite a bit more than “socialism,” since it refers to institutions that really existed before it came into being. Still, it does not signify anything that can be rigorously defined and clearly delineated historically. Thus, like socialism, it is a metaphysical far more than an empirical term. And like socialism, its meaning ranges from the ethical to the institutional spheres, when it does not combine and confuse the two. Morally, it carries a positive charge of dynamism, but a far stronger negative charge of individual greed and social exploitation. Institutionally, it ranges from the extreme laissez-faire policies of nineteenth-century Manchester liberalism—what its critics call “wild” or “untamed capitalism”—to a whole gamut of twentieth-century modes of state regulation in the service of the welfare state. Historically, it covers various degrees of development, from sixteenth and seventeenth century merchant and “comprador” capitalism, to the classical industrial system, to the postindustrial service-dominated economy. And sociologically, within the twentieth century, its ranges from the predominantly free market of the United States, to the more
and “social market” economies of the European Community, to the state-industrial corporatism of Japan.

zh: 把这一切都称为“资本主义”，虽然并非毫无意义，但对于理解这个“系统”如何运作、其制度如何产生，帮助不大。事实上，从实用目的看，如果我们能抛弃资本主义一词及其对立面社会主义，那将是一件幸事。但这不太可能，因为在各种资本主义背后确实存在一个核心现实——这个核心恰恰是完整社会主义的镜像。因为所有可以被合情合理地称为资本主义的社会，都在某种程度上接受私有制、利润和市场的制度。但与此同时，这些制度总是在某种程度上与民主政治形式中所蕴含的平等理想相冲突，而这些民主政治形式是“资本主义”经济最优运行所必需的。因此，用亚历山大·季诺维也夫的词汇来说，“资本主义”（
）与“社会主义”（
）的两极性，虽然在分析上模糊不清，却仍然保持其道德吸引力。两者如同连体双胞胎，被财产这个永远敏感的问题在脊柱处连在一起。
en: To call all of this “capitalism,” though not actually meaningless, is not very helpful in understanding how the “system” works, or how its institutions came into being. Indeed, for practical purposes it would be a blessing if we could get rid of the term capitalism, together with its polar opposite, socialism. But this is not a likely prospect, since there does exist a core reality behind the various capitalisms—a core which is precisely the mirror image of integral socialism. For all the societies that may plausibly be called capitalist accept, in some measure, the institutions of private property, profit, and the market. Yet at the same time these institutions always conflict, in some measure, with the egalitarian ideals embedded in the democratic political forms necessary to the optimal functioning of the “capitalist” economies. So the polarity of “cap-ism” and “soc-ism,” to use Aleksandr Zinoviev’s vocabulary, while analytically obfuscating, nonetheless retains its moral magnetism. The two, like Siamese twins, remain joined at the spine by the eternally raw issue of property.

zh: 一旦整个欧洲在1900年前后接受了这个新的总体化术语“资本主义”，它便立即被归入右派的政治标签之下。因为这个术语以负面含义为主，使它在民主政治中成为一种负担，而民主政治的道德高地总是被左派占据。候选人很少标榜自己是资本的捍卫者，而关心劳工、公开信奉社会主义理想，通常是一种可接受的、而且往往是有利的立场。
en: Once all of Europe had adopted the new totalizing term “capitalism,” around 1900, it immediately fell under the political rubric of the Right. For the term’s predominantly negative connotation made it a liability in democratic politics, where the moral high ground is invariably occupied by the Left. Candidates rarely advertise themselves as champions of capital, whereas concern for labor and the public profession of socialist ideals is usually an admissible, and often an advantageous, stance.

zh: 因此，到1914年，一个双重归并过程已经发生：右派一边排列着资本主义、无拘无束的个人主义、民族主义、军国主义和社会等级制；左派一边排列着社会主义、经济理性、国际主义、和平与平等。于是，舞台已经搭好，等待着资本主义与社会主义之间那场伟大的“交锋”（
）、那场将支配我们短二十世纪的世界历史冲突。
en: And so, by 1914, a dual process of amalgamation had occurred: On the Right were aligned capitalism, unbridled individualism, nationalism, militarism, and social hierarchy; and on the Left were arrayed socialism, economic rationality, internationalism, peace, and equality. The stage was thus set for the great
, the world-historical clash, between capitalism and socialism that would dominate our short twentieth century.

zh: 然而，这场冲突并未发生在指定的世界历史地点——成熟的工业西方，也没有按照正当的历史程序、通过社会革命的动力发生。黑格尔的“理性的狡计”
对所有历史棋子开了一个乖戾的玩笑。因为世界上第一场社会主义革命在欧洲最落后的国家俄国取得了胜利；它不是通过俄国内部过程的逻辑，而是由于外部战争这一“偶然的”或机缘性的因素。其结果便是一个悖论：在一个绝大多数人口是农民的国家里发生了一场无产阶级革命。
en: This clash, however, did not occur in the designated world-historical place, the mature industrial West, nor according to proper historical procedures, through the dynamic of social revolution. Hegel’s Cunning of Reason

played a perverse trick on all its historical pawns. For the world’s first socialist revolution triumphed in the most backward nation of Europe, Russia; and it did so not through the logic of Russia’s internal processes, but because of the “accidental,” or contingent, factor of external war. And the result was the paradox of a proletarian revolution in an overwhelmingly peasant country.

zh: 这种不顺遂的结果常被用来为革命开脱其后来显而易见的缺陷，甚至暗示落后的俄国以某种方式破坏了历史的逻辑。换言之，布尔什维克革命的问题不在于完整社会主义，而在于俄国。但事实上根本不存在什么悖论；十月出人意料的结果的意义仅仅在于，作为其基础的马克思主义理论的正式信条是错误的。
en: This untoward outcome has often been taken to exculpate the Revolution from its obvious later shortcomings, or even to suggest that backward Russia somehow spoiled the logic of history. In other words, the problem with the Bolshevik Revolution was not integral socialism; it was Russia. But in fact there is no paradox at all; the significance of the unexpected results of October is simply that the formal tenets of the Marxist theory underlying it are wrong.

zh: 尽管如此，十月确实有其逻辑，只是并非其作者正式学说中的逻辑。而这个逻辑与马克思主义的深层结构相当契合：匮乏与苦难的自我丰富异化——这种动力在1914年之后表现为现代总体战争的破坏。表面悖论的“理性”特征就在于此。因为所有马克思主义革命，从列宁的革命到毛泽东和胡志明的革命，从第一次世界大战到第二次世界大战，都产生于落后国家，并在战争冲击下发生。这本身就是它们的逻辑，而绝非偶然。
en: Nevertheless, October does have its logic, though not that of its authors’ formal doctrine. And this logic is quite compatible with Marxism’s deeper structure: the self-enriching alienation of privation and suffering, as this dynamic was expressed after 1914 in the devastation of modern, total war. Therein lies the “rational” character of the apparent paradox. For all Marxist revolutions, from that of Lenin to those of Mao and Ho Chi Minh, and from the-First World War to the Second, were produced in backward countries and under the impact of war. This
their logic, and not an accident at all.
